sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第218卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, volume 218
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 218.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十四】 起柔兆涒灘五月，至九月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 34] From the fifth month of rouzhao toushan to the ninth month, less than one full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 34] From the fifth month of rouzhao toushan through the ninth month—less than a full year.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝上之下至德元年（

translations.literal: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Suzong, the Civilized, Martial, Virtuous, Great Sage, Great Proclaimer, and Filial—first year of Zhide (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Suzong (posthumous titles: Civilized, Martial, Virtuous, Great Sage, Great Proclaimer, Filial)—first year of Zhide (

sentences.zh: 丙申，公元七五六年）

translations.literal: bingshen, CE 756)
translations.idiomatic: bingshen, AD 756)

sentences.zh: 五月，丁巳，炅眾潰，走保南陽，賊就圍之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day dingsi, Lu Hui's army was routed and fled to defend Nanyang; the rebels thereupon besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingsi day, Lu Hui's forces collapsed in defeat and withdrew to hold Nanyang, where the rebels promptly laid siege.

sentences.zh: 太常卿張垍薦夷陵太守虢王巨有勇略，上征吳王祗為太僕卿，以巨為陳留、譙郡太守、河南節度使，兼統嶺南節度使何履光、黔中節度使趙國珍、南陽節度使魯炅。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Yi recommended that Yiling Administrator Prince of Guo Ju had courage and strategy; the emperor summoned Prince of Wu Zhi to serve as Minister of the Imperial Stud and appointed Ju as Administrator of Chenliu and Qiao commanderies and Military Commissioner of Henan, with concurrent command over Military Commissioner of Lingnan He Lüguang, Military Commissioner of Qianzhong Zhao Guozhen, and Military Commissioner of Nanyang Lu Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Yi recommended Yiling Administrator Prince of Guo Ju as a man of courage and stratagem. The emperor recalled Prince of Wu Zhi to appoint him Minister of the Imperial Stud, made Ju Administrator of Chenliu and Qiao and Military Commissioner of Henan, and placed him over Lingnan Commissioner He Lüguang, Qianzhong Commissioner Zhao Guozhen, and Nanyang Commissioner Lu Hui.

sentences.zh: 國珍，本牂柯夷也。

translations.literal: Guozhen was originally a Yi of Zangge.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was originally a tribal chieftain of Zangge.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，巨引兵自藍田出，趣南陽。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Ju led troops out from Lantian and hastened toward Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day, Ju marched out from Lantian toward Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 賊聞之，解圍走。

translations.literal: When the rebels heard of it, they lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard he was coming, they broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 令狐潮復引兵攻雍丘。

translations.literal: Linghu Chao again led troops to attack Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao once more led his army against Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 潮與張巡有舊，於城下相勞苦如平生，潮因說巡曰：「天下事去矣，足下堅守危城，欲誰為乎？」

translations.literal: Chao and Zhang Xun were old acquaintances; below the walls they exchanged greetings as in former days, and Chao thereupon urged Xun, saying, "The affairs of the empire are already lost—why do you stubbornly hold this perilous city, and for whom?"
translations.idiomatic: Chao and Zhang Xun were old friends. Below the walls they exchanged courtesies as in days gone by, and Chao then tried to persuade Xun: "The empire is finished. Why do you cling to this doomed city—and for whose sake?"

sentences.zh: 巡曰：「足下平生以忠義自許，今日之舉，忠義何在！」

translations.literal: Xun said, "You have always prided yourself on loyalty and righteousness—where are loyalty and righteousness in what you do today!"
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied, "You have always styled yourself a man of loyalty and righteousness. Where is either loyalty or righteousness in what you do today?"

sentences.zh: 潮慚而退。

translations.literal: Chao, ashamed, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chao, abashed, drew back and left.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀、李光弼還常山，史思明收散卒數萬踵其後。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi returned to Changshan; Shi Siming gathered several tens of thousands of scattered troops and followed close behind.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi withdrew to Changshan, with Shi Siming gathering tens of thousands of stragglers and pressing close on their heels.

sentences.zh: 子儀選驍騎更挑戰，三日，至行唐，賊疲，乃退。

translations.literal: Ziyi selected crack cavalry and repeatedly offered battle; after three days they reached Xingtang, and when the rebels were exhausted they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi picked elite horsemen and harried them with repeated challenges. After three days they reached Xingtang; once the rebels were worn down, Siming pulled back.

sentences.zh: 子儀乘之，又敗之於沙河。

translations.literal: Ziyi pressed the advantage and again defeated them at Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi pressed the pursuit and routed them again at Shahe.

sentences.zh: 蔡希德至洛陽，安祿山復使將步騎二萬人北就思明，又使牛廷玠發范陽等郡兵萬餘人助思明，合五萬餘人，而同羅、曳落河居五分之一。

translations.literal: Cai Xide reached Luoyang; An Lushan again sent him to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry north to join Siming, and also had Niu Tingjie raise more than ten thousand troops from Fanyang and other commanderies to assist Siming, totaling more than fifty thousand men, of whom the Tongluo and yeluohe made up one-fifth.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Xide reached Luoyang, An Lushan again ordered him north with twenty thousand foot and horse to reinforce Siming, and had Niu Tingjie levy more than ten thousand men from Fanyang and neighboring districts. Together they numbered over fifty thousand, one-fifth of them Tongluo and yeluohe troops.

sentences.zh: 子儀至恆陽，思明隨至，子儀深溝高壘以待之；

translations.literal: Ziyi reached Hengyang; Siming followed close behind, and Ziyi dug deep ditches and raised high ramparts to await him;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi advanced to Hengyang with Siming hard on his trail. Ziyi entrenched himself behind deep trenches and high walls;

sentences.zh: 賊來則守，去則追之，晝則耀兵，夜斫其營，賊不得休息。

translations.literal: when the rebels came he defended, when they left he pursued; by day he displayed his troops, by night he raided their camps—the rebels could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: when the rebels came he held firm, when they withdrew he harried them; by day he paraded his strength, by night he struck their camps, giving the enemy no respite.

sentences.zh: 數日，子儀、光弼議曰。

translations.literal: After several days, Ziyi and Guangbi deliberated, saying,
translations.idiomatic: After several days, Ziyi and Guangbi conferred:

sentences.zh: 「賊倦矣，可以出戰。」

translations.literal: "The rebels are weary; we can give battle."
translations.idiomatic: "The enemy is exhausted—we can take the field."

sentences.zh: 壬午，戰於嘉山，大破之，斬首四萬級，捕虜千餘人。

translations.literal: On the day renwu they fought at Jiashan and inflicted a great defeat, beheading forty thousand and capturing more than a thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day they fought at Jiashan and won a crushing victory, taking forty thousand heads and more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 思明墜馬，露髻跣足步走，至暮，杖折槍歸營，奔於博陵；

translations.literal: Siming fell from his horse, bared his topknot, and fled on foot barefoot; by evening, leaning on a broken spear, he returned to camp and fled to Boling;
translations.idiomatic: Siming was thrown from his horse, hair loose and feet bare, and fled on foot. By evening, leaning on a broken spear, he limped back to camp and then ran for Boling;

sentences.zh: 光弼就圍之，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Guangbi pressed on to besiege him, and the army's morale soared.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi pressed the siege, and government morale soared.

sentences.zh: 於是河北十餘郡皆殺賊守將而降。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than ten commanderies north of the Yellow River all killed the rebel garrison commanders and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen Hebei commanderies now killed their rebel garrison commanders and came over.

sentences.zh: 漁陽路再絕，賊往來者皆輕騎竊過，多為官軍所獲，將士家在漁陽者無不搖心。

translations.literal: The route to Fanyang was again cut; rebels traveling back and forth all stole through with light cavalry and were mostly captured by government troops, and every soldier with family in Fanyang was shaken at heart.
translations.idiomatic: The road to Fanyang was severed again. Rebel couriers could only slip through with light cavalry and were mostly intercepted. Every soldier with kin in Fanyang felt his heart quail.

sentences.zh: 祿山大懼，召高尚、嚴莊詬之曰：「汝數年教我反，以為萬全。

translations.literal: Lushan was greatly afraid; he summoned Gao Shang and Yan Zhuang and reviled them, saying, "For years you urged me to rebel, claiming it was perfectly safe.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was terrified. He summoned Gao Shang and Yan Zhuang and berated them: "For years you urged me to rebel, promising complete safety.

sentences.zh: 今守潼關，數月不能進，北路已絕，諸軍四合，吾所有者止汴、鄭數州而已，萬全何在？

translations.literal: Now we hold Tong Pass and for months cannot advance; the northern route is already cut off, and armies converge from all sides—what I hold is only a few prefectures such as Bian and Zheng. Where is this 'perfect safety'?"
translations.idiomatic: Now we sit at Tong Pass for months without advancing. The northern route is gone, armies close in from every quarter, and I hold only Bian, Zheng, and a few other prefectures. Where is your 'complete safety'?"

sentences.zh: 汝自今勿來見我！」

translations.literal: From now on, do not come to see me again!"
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, do not come before me again!"

sentences.zh: 尚、莊懼，數日不敢見。

translations.literal: Shang and Zhuang were afraid and for several days did not dare to appear.
translations.idiomatic: Shang and Zhuang were terrified and stayed away for days.

sentences.zh: 田乾真自關下來，為尚、莊說祿山曰：「自古帝王經營大業，皆有勝敗，豈能一舉而成！

translations.literal: Tian Qianzhen came down from the pass and spoke to Lushan on behalf of Shang and Zhuang, saying, "Since antiquity every emperor who built a great enterprise has known victory and defeat—how could success be achieved in a single stroke!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Qianzhen came down from the pass and pleaded with Lushan for Shang and Zhuang: "Since antiquity, every ruler who built a great enterprise has known both victory and defeat. Who ever won everything in one stroke?

sentences.zh: 今四方軍壘雖多，皆新募烏合之眾，未更行陳，豈能敵我薊北勁銳之兵，何足深憂！

translations.literal: Though enemy camps are many on all sides, they are all newly recruited rabble who have never drilled in formation—how can they stand against our crack troops from north of Ji? What is there to worry about so deeply!
translations.idiomatic: The enemy camps are many, but they are all fresh levies and rabble who have never drilled in formation. How can they match our crack troops from north of Ji? There is no cause for such deep alarm!

sentences.zh: 尚、莊皆佐命元勳，陛下一旦絕之，使諸將聞之，誰不內懼！

translations.literal: Shang and Zhuang are both founding ministers of the highest merit—if Your Majesty cuts them off at a stroke, when the generals hear of it, who will not be inwardly afraid!
translations.idiomatic: Shang and Zhuang are founding ministers of the first rank. If Your Majesty casts them off in a moment, every general who hears of it will quake inwardly!

sentences.zh: 若上下離心，臣竊為陛下危之！」

translations.literal: If superiors and subordinates lose heart for one another, your servant ventures to deem Your Majesty in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: If ruler and commanders lose faith in one another, I fear for Your Majesty's safety!"

sentences.zh: 祿山喜曰：「阿浩，汝能豁我心事。」

translations.literal: Lushan said with pleasure, "Ahao, you can clear the troubles from my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Lushan brightened: "Ahao, you know how to ease my mind."

sentences.zh: 即召尚、莊，置酒酣宴，自為之歌以侑酒，待之如初。

translations.literal: He at once summoned Shang and Zhuang, set out wine for a hearty banquet, himself sang a song to accompany the cups, and treated them as before.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Shang and Zhuang at once, spread a feast, sang for them himself to keep the wine flowing, and treated them as he always had.

sentences.zh: 阿浩，乾真小字也。

translations.literal: Ahao was Qianzhen's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Ahao was Qianzhen's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 祿山議棄洛陽，走歸范陽，計未決。

translations.literal: Lushan debated abandoning Luoyang and fleeing back to Fanyang, but the plan was not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan debated abandoning Luoyang and fleeing back to Fanyang, but could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下以楊國忠驕縱召亂，莫不切齒。

translations.literal: At this time the empire blamed Yang Guozhong's arrogance and indulgence for having provoked the rebellion, and all gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the empire, men blamed Yang Guozhong's arrogance and excess for having provoked the rebellion, and gnashed their teeth at his name.

sentences.zh: 又，祿山起兵以誅國忠為名，王思禮密說哥舒翰，使抗表請誅國忠，翰不應。

translations.literal: Moreover, Lushan had raised his army under the banner of executing Guozhong; Wang Silun secretly urged Geshu Han to submit a memorial requesting Guozhong's execution, but Han would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had moreover raised his banners in the name of executing Guozhong. Wang Silun secretly urged Geshu Han to memorialize for Guozhong's death, but Han refused.

sentences.zh: 思禮又請以三十騎劫取以來，至潼關殺之。

translations.literal: Silun again asked to take thirty horsemen, seize him by force, bring him to Tong Pass, and kill him there.
translations.idiomatic: Silun then proposed taking thirty horsemen to seize him by force and execute him at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 翰曰：「如此，乃翰反，非祿山也。」

translations.literal: Han said, "If we did that, it would be Han rebelling, not Lushan."
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "If I did that, it would be I who rebelled—not Lushan."

sentences.zh: 或說國忠：「今朝廷重兵盡在翰手，翰若援旗西指，於公豈不危哉！」

translations.literal: Someone said to Guozhong, "Now the court's main armies are all in Han's hands—if Han should raise his banner and march west, would you not be in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Guozhong: "The court's main armies are all in Han's hands. If he turned his banners west, would you not be in mortal danger?"

sentences.zh: 國忠大懼，乃奏：「潼關大軍雖盛，而後無繼，萬一失利，京師可憂。

translations.literal: Guozhong was greatly afraid and thereupon memorialized, "Though the army at Tong Pass is strong, there is no reserve behind it; if it should suffer defeat, the capital would be at risk.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was terrified and memorialized: "Though the Tong Pass army is strong, it has no reserve behind it. One defeat, and the capital itself is at risk.

sentences.zh: 請選監牧小兒三千於苑中訓練。」

translations.literal: I request that three thousand boys from the imperial stud be selected and trained within the park."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that three thousand lads from the imperial stud be selected and drilled in the park."

sentences.zh: 上許之，使劍南軍將李福德等領之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and had the Jiannan army officer Li Fude and others lead them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and put them under Jiannan general Li Fude and others.

sentences.zh: 又募萬人屯灞上，令所親杜乾運將之，名為御賊，實備翰也。

translations.literal: He also recruited ten thousand men to encamp at Bashang, putting his confidant Du Qianyun in command—nominally to resist the rebels, but in truth to guard against Han.
translations.idiomatic: He also raised ten thousand men at Bashang under his confidant Du Qianyun—nominally to resist the rebels, in truth to guard against Han.

sentences.zh: 翰聞之，亦恐為國忠所圖，乃表請灞上軍隸潼關。

translations.literal: When Han heard of this, he too feared a plot by Guozhong and memorialized requesting that the Bashang army be placed under Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Han, hearing this, feared Guozhong meant to destroy him and memorialized that the Bashang force be placed under Tong Pass command.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸未，召杜乾運詣關，因事斬之；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day guiwei, he summoned Du Qianyun to the pass and, on a pretext, beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guiwei day, he summoned Du Qianyun to the pass and, on a pretext, executed him;

sentences.zh: 國忠益懼。

translations.literal: Guozhong grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong grew still more afraid.

sentences.zh: 會有告崔乾祐在陝，兵不滿四千，皆羸弱無備，上遣使趣哥舒翰進兵復陝、洛。

translations.literal: It happened that someone reported Cui Qianyu was at Shan with fewer than four thousand troops, all weak and unprepared; the emperor sent envoys urging Geshu Han to advance and recover Shan and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Cui Qianyu held Shan with fewer than four thousand men, all weak and unprepared. The emperor sent envoys urging Geshu Han to advance and recover Shan and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 翰奏曰：「祿山久習用兵，今始為逆，豈肯無備！

translations.literal: Han memorialized, "Lushan has long been skilled in warfare; now that he has just risen in rebellion, how would he be unprepared!
translations.idiomatic: Han memorialized: "Lushan has commanded armies for years. Having just risen in rebellion, would he truly leave himself unguarded?

sentences.zh: 是必羸師以誘我。

translations.literal: This must be a display of weak troops to lure us.
translations.idiomatic: This can only be a display of weakness to lure us in.

sentences.zh: 若往，正墮其計中。

translations.literal: If we go, we will fall straight into their trap.
translations.idiomatic: If we march out, we walk straight into their trap.

sentences.zh: 且賊遠來，利在速戰；

translations.literal: Moreover, the rebels have come from afar—their advantage lies in swift battle;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels have marched far from home; their advantage lies in a quick fight.

sentences.zh: 官軍據險以扼之，利在堅守。

translations.literal: the government army holds the defiles to choke them—their advantage lies in steadfast defense.
translations.idiomatic: Our army holds the defiles; our advantage lies in holding firm.

sentences.zh: 況賊殘虐失眾，兵勢日蹙，將有內變；

translations.literal: Moreover, the rebels are cruel and have lost the people's hearts; their military strength daily contracts, and internal strife will arise;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are brutal and losing the people's hearts. Their strength shrinks daily, and internal strife will come.

sentences.zh: 因而乘之，可不戰擒也。

translations.literal: seize the moment and we can capture them without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Seize that moment, and we can take them without a battle.

sentences.zh: 要在成功，何必務速！

translations.literal: What matters is success—why must we hurry!
translations.idiomatic: What matters is success—why insist on speed?

sentences.zh: 今諸道徵兵尚多未集，請且待之。」

translations.literal: The levies from the various circuits have not yet mostly assembled—please wait awhile."
translations.idiomatic: The levies from the circuits have not yet mostly arrived. I beg Your Majesty to wait."

sentences.zh: 郭子儀、李光弼亦上言：「請引兵北取范阻，覆其巢穴，質賊黨妻子以招之，賊必內潰。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi also submitted, "We request to lead troops north to take Fanyang, overturn their nest, hold the wives and children of the rebel party as hostages to summon them, and the rebels will surely collapse from within.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi also wrote: "Let us march north on Fanyang, overturn their nest, and hold rebel families as hostages to summon their surrender. The rebels will collapse from within.

sentences.zh: 潼關大軍，帷應固守以弊之，不可輕出。」

translations.literal: The great army at Tong Pass should only hold fast and wear them down—it must not sally lightly."
translations.idiomatic: The Tong Pass army should only hold fast and wear them down. It must not sally lightly."

sentences.zh: 國忠疑翰謀己，言於上，以賊方無備，而翰逗留，將失機會。

translations.literal: Guozhong suspected Han was plotting against him and spoke to the emperor, saying the rebels were presently unprepared while Han lingered and would miss the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong suspected Han plotted against him and told the emperor the rebels were unprepared while Han dallied and would miss his chance.

sentences.zh: 上以為然，續遣中使趣之，項背相望。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct and repeatedly sent palace envoys to urge him on, one after another in endless succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent palace envoys one after another to hurry him—envoys stretching back to back along the road.

sentences.zh: 翰不得已，撫膺慟哭；

translations.literal: Han had no choice; he beat his breast and wept bitterly;
translations.idiomatic: Han had no choice. He beat his breast and wept;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，引兵出關。

translations.literal: on the day bingxu he led his army out of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: on bingxu day he led his army out of the pass.

sentences.zh: 己丑，遇崔乾祐之軍於靈寶西原。

translations.literal: On the day jichou he encountered Cui Qianyu's army on the western plain of Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day he met Cui Qianyu's army on the western plain of Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 乾祐據險以待之，南薄山，北阻河，隘道七十里。

translations.literal: Qianyu held the defiles to await him—mountains pressing close on the south, the river blocking the north, a narrow road seventy li long.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyu held the defiles to receive him: mountains close on the south, the river on the north, a narrow road seventy li long.

sentences.zh: 庚寅。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day.

sentences.zh: 官軍與乾祐會戰。

translations.literal: The government army joined battle with Qianyu.
translations.idiomatic: The government army joined battle with Qianyu.

sentences.zh: 乾祐伏兵於險，翰與田良丘浮舟中流以觀軍勢，見乾祐兵少，趣諸軍使進。

translations.literal: Qianyu hid troops in the defiles; Han and Tian Liangqiu floated a boat midstream to observe the army's disposition, saw that Qianyu's troops were few, and urged the armies to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyu hid troops in the defiles. Han and Tian Liangqiu floated a boat midstream to survey the field, saw Qianyu's force was small, and ordered the armies forward.

sentences.zh: 王思禮等將精兵五萬居前，龐忠等將餘兵十萬繼之，翰以兵三萬登河北阜望之，鳴鼓以助其勢。

translations.literal: Wang Silun and others led fifty thousand elite troops in the van; Pang Zhong and others led the remaining hundred thousand in the rear; Han with thirty thousand men climbed the north-bank heights to watch and beat drums to swell their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Silun led fifty thousand elite troops in the van; Pang Zhong led the remaining hundred thousand behind. Han took thirty thousand men onto the north-bank heights to watch and beat drums to swell their momentum.

sentences.zh: 乾祐所出兵不過萬人，什什伍伍，散如列星，或疏或密，或前或卻，官軍望而笑之。

translations.literal: The troops Qianyu sent out were no more than ten thousand, scattered in squads of ten and fives like stars in a row, now sparse now dense, now advancing now retreating—the government army looked on and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyu sent out no more than ten thousand men, scattered in squads of ten and five like stars in a row—now sparse, now dense, now advancing, now falling back. The government troops looked on and laughed.

sentences.zh: 乾祐嚴精兵，陳於其後。

translations.literal: Qianyu arrayed crack troops in tight formation behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Behind them Qianyu held his crack troops in tight formation.

sentences.zh: 兵既交，賊偃旗如欲遁者，官軍懈，不為備。

translations.literal: Once the armies clashed, the rebels lowered their banners as if about to flee; the government army relaxed and took no precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Once battle was joined, the rebels lowered their banners as if to flee. The government army relaxed and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 須臾，伏兵發，賊乘高下木石，擊殺士卒甚眾。

translations.literal: In a moment the ambush struck; the rebels hurled timber and stone from the heights, killing very many soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the ambush struck. From the heights the rebels rained timber and stone, slaughtering great numbers.

sentences.zh: 道隘，士卒如束，槍槊不得用。

translations.literal: The road was narrow; soldiers were packed like bundles and could not use spears or halberds.
translations.idiomatic: The road was so narrow the men were packed like cordwood; spears and halberds were useless.

sentences.zh: 翰以氈車駕馬為前驅，欲以沖賊。

translations.literal: Han used felt-covered wagons drawn by horses as vanguard, intending to charge the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent felt-covered wagons drawn by horses in the van, hoping to smash through the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 日過中，東風暴急，乾祐以草車數十乘塞氈車之前，縱火焚之，煙焰所被，官軍不能開目，妄自相殺，謂賊在煙中，聚弓弩而射之。

translations.literal: Past midday a violent east wind arose; Qianyu blocked the felt wagons with several dozen straw carts, set them afire, and where smoke and flame spread the government troops could not open their eyes; they killed one another at random, thinking the rebels were in the smoke, and massed crossbows to shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Past midday a violent east wind sprang up. Qianyu blocked the felt wagons with dozens of straw carts and set them ablaze. Where smoke and flame spread, government troops could not open their eyes. They killed one another at random, thinking the enemy was in the smoke, and massed crossbows to shoot into the murk.

sentences.zh: 日幕，矢盡，乃知無賊。

translations.literal: At day's end their arrows were spent, and only then did they know there were no rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At day's end their arrows were spent, and only then did they know there were no rebels there.

sentences.zh: 乾祐遣同羅精騎自南山過，出官軍之後擊之，官軍首尾駭亂，不知所備，於是大敗；

translations.literal: Qianyu sent Tongluo crack cavalry around from the southern mountains to strike the government army from behind; front and rear were thrown into panic and knew not what to guard against, and so they suffered a great defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Qianyu sent Tongluo crack cavalry around from the southern mountains to strike the government army from behind. Front and rear panicked, knowing not what to guard against, and the army was utterly broken;

sentences.zh: 或棄甲竄匿山谷，或相擠排入河溺死，囂聲振天地，賊乘勝蹙之。

translations.literal: some cast off armor and fled into mountain valleys, some were crushed and pushed into the river and drowned—the clamor shook heaven and earth, and the rebels pressed the victory hard.
translations.idiomatic: some cast off armor and fled into the valleys, others were crushed and pushed into the river to drown. The uproar shook heaven and earth as the rebels pressed the rout.

sentences.zh: 後軍見前軍敗，皆自潰，河北軍望之亦潰，瞬息間，兩岸皆空。

translations.literal: The rear army saw the van defeated and all broke on their own; the Hebei troops on the north bank, seeing this, broke too—in an instant both banks were empty.
translations.idiomatic: The rear saw the van collapse and broke on its own. The Hebei troops on the north bank, seeing this, broke too. In an instant both banks were empty.

sentences.zh: 翰獨與麾下百餘騎走，自首陽山西渡河入關。

translations.literal: Han alone with a little more than a hundred horsemen of his staff fled, crossing the river west of Shouyang Mountain to enter the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Han alone fled with a little more than a hundred horsemen of his staff, crossing the river west of Shouyang Mountain to re-enter the pass.

sentences.zh: 關外先為三塹，皆廣二丈，深丈，人馬墜其中，須臾而滿；

translations.literal: Outside the pass three ditches had been dug beforehand, each two zhang wide and one zhang deep; men and horses fell into them and in a moment they were filled;
translations.idiomatic: Outside the pass three ditches had been dug, each two zhang wide and one zhang deep. Men and horses tumbled in and filled them in moments;

sentences.zh: 餘眾踐之以度，士卒得入關者才八千餘人。

translations.literal: the rest trampled across atop them to get through, and soldiers who actually entered the pass numbered only a little more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: the rest trampled across atop the fallen to get through. Only a little more than eight thousand soldiers actually made it inside the pass.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，乾祐進攻潼關，克之。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Qianyu advanced to attack Tong Pass and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day, Qianyu advanced on Tong Pass and took it.

sentences.zh: 翰至關西驛，揭榜收散卒，欲復守潼關。

translations.literal: Han reached the Guanxi post station, posted notices to gather scattered troops, and wished again to defend Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Han reached the Guanxi post station, posted notices to gather scattered troops, and hoped again to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 蕃將火拔歸仁等以百餘騎圍驛，入謂翰曰：「賊至矣，請公上馬。」

translations.literal: The foreign general Huoba Guiren and others with a little more than a hundred horsemen surrounded the post station, entered, and said to Han, "The rebels have come—please mount, sir."
translations.idiomatic: The foreign general Huoba Guiren and others surrounded the station with a little more than a hundred horsemen, entered, and said to Han, "The rebels are here, sir—please mount."

sentences.zh: 翰上馬出驛，歸仁帥眾叩頭曰：「公以二十萬眾一戰棄之，何面目復見天子！

translations.literal: Han mounted and left the station; Guiren led the crowd in kowtowing and said, "Sir, you threw away two hundred thousand men in a single battle—what face have you to see the Son of Heaven again!
translations.idiomatic: Han mounted and left the station. Guiren led the men in kowtowing: "Sir, you threw away two hundred thousand men in a single battle—what face have you to see the Son of Heaven again!

sentences.zh: 且公不見高仙芝，封常清乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, have you not seen Gao Xianzhi and Feng Changqing?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen what became of Gao Xianzhi and Feng Changqing?

sentences.zh: 請公東行。」

translations.literal: We beg you, sir, to go east."
translations.idiomatic: We beg you, sir, to go east."

sentences.zh: 翰不可，欲下馬。

translations.literal: Han would not agree and wished to dismount.
translations.idiomatic: Han refused and tried to dismount.

sentences.zh: 歸仁以毛縻其足於馬腹，及諸將不從者，皆執之以東。

translations.literal: Guiren bound his feet to the horse's belly with a thong, and all the generals who would not follow were seized and taken east.
translations.idiomatic: Guiren lashed his feet to the horse's belly with a thong. Every general who would not follow was seized and driven east.

sentences.zh: 會賊將田乾真已至，遂降之，俱送洛陽。

translations.literal: It happened that the rebel general Tian Qianzhen had already arrived; they thereupon surrendered to him and were all sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Tian Qianzhen had already arrived. They surrendered to him and were all sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 安祿山問翰曰：「汝常輕我，今定何如？」

translations.literal: An Lushan asked Han, "You always looked down on me—how do matters stand now?"
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan asked Han, "You always looked down on me—how do matters stand now?"

sentences.zh: 翰伏地對曰：「臣肉眼不識聖人。

translations.literal: Han prostrated himself and replied, "Your servant's fleshly eyes did not recognize a sage.
translations.idiomatic: Han prostrated himself and said, "These mortal eyes of mine failed to recognize a sage.

sentences.zh: 今天下未平，李光弼在常山，李祗在東平，魯炅在南陽，陛下留臣，使以尺書招之，不日皆下矣。」

translations.literal: The empire is not yet pacified—Li Guangbi is at Changshan, Li Zhi at Dongping, Lu Hui at Nanyang. If Your Majesty keeps me and lets me summon them with a brief letter, in no many days they will all submit."
translations.idiomatic: The empire is not yet pacified. Li Guangbi holds Changshan, Li Zhi holds Dongping, Lu Hui holds Nanyang. Keep me, Your Majesty, and let me summon them with a brief letter—they will all submit in no time."

sentences.zh: 祿山大喜，以翰為司空、同平章事。

translations.literal: Lushan was greatly pleased and appointed Han Minister of Works and Fellow Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was delighted and made Han Minister of Works and Fellow Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 謂火拔歸仁曰：「汝叛主，不忠不義。」

translations.literal: He said to Huoba Guiren, "You betrayed your lord—disloyal and unrighteous."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Huoba Guiren, "You betrayed your lord—faithless and without honor."

sentences.zh: 執而斬之。

translations.literal: He seized him and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had him seized and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 翰以書招諸將，皆復書責之。

translations.literal: Han used letters to summon the generals; all wrote back rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Han wrote letters summoning the generals; every one wrote back to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 祿山知無效，乃囚諸苑中。

translations.literal: Lushan knew it was useless and thereupon imprisoned him in the park.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan saw it was useless and had him imprisoned in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 潼關既敗，於是河東、華陰、馮翊、上洛防禦使皆棄郡走，所在守兵皆散。

translations.literal: Once Tong Pass fell, the defense commissioners of Hedong, Huayin, Fengyi, and Shangluo all abandoned their commanderies and fled, and garrison troops everywhere scattered.
translations.idiomatic: With Tong Pass lost, the defense commissioners of Hedong, Huayin, Fengyi, and Shangluo all abandoned their posts and fled, and garrisons everywhere melted away.

sentences.zh: 是日，翰麾下來告急，上不時召見，但遣李福德等將監牧兵赴潼關。

translations.literal: That day, Han's subordinates came with urgent reports, but the emperor did not summon them promptly and only sent Li Fude and others leading the stud-guard troops to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: That day Han's officers brought urgent word, but the emperor would not see them in time and only sent Li Fude with the stud-guard troops toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 及暮，平安火不至，上始懼。

translations.literal: By evening the peace beacons had not arrived, and the emperor first grew afraid.
translations.idiomatic: By evening the peace beacons had not come, and the emperor began to fear.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，召宰相謀之。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, he summoned the chief ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day he summoned the chief ministers to counsel.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠自以身領劍南，聞安祿山反，即令副使崔圓陰具儲偫，以備有急投之，至是首唱幸蜀之策。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong himself held the post of Military Commissioner of Jiannan; when he heard An Lushan had rebelled, he at once had Vice Commissioner Cui Yuan secretly prepare stores against emergency flight thither, and now he was first to urge the plan of taking refuge in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong himself held Jiannan as military commissioner. When Lushan rebelled he had already ordered Vice Commissioner Cui Yuan to stock supplies in secret against a sudden flight there. Now he was first to urge refuge in Shu.

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，國忠集百官於朝堂，惶懅流涕；

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Guozhong gathered the hundred officials in the audience hall, fearful and weeping;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Guozhong gathered the officials in the audience hall, weeping in terror;

sentences.zh: 問以策略，皆唯唯不對。

translations.literal: he asked them for strategy, and all murmured assent without answering.
translations.idiomatic: he asked them for counsel, and all murmured without a word.

sentences.zh: 國忠曰：「人告祿山反狀已十年，上下之信。

translations.literal: Guozhong said, "People have reported Lushan's rebellious intent for ten years, yet court and people did not believe.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong said, "For ten years men reported Lushan's rebellious intent, yet neither court nor people would believe it.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，非宰相之過。」

translations.literal: Today's affair is not the fault of the chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: What has happened today is not the chief minister's fault."

sentences.zh: 仗下，士民掠擾奔走，不知所之，市裡蕭條。

translations.literal: Below the hall, soldiers and commoners looted and fled in confusion, not knowing where to go; the markets were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Below the hall soldiers and townspeople looted and fled in every direction; the markets stood empty.

sentences.zh: 國忠使韓、虢入宮，勸上入蜀。

translations.literal: Guozhong had the Ladies of Han and Guo enter the palace to urge the emperor to go into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong sent the Ladies of Han and Guo into the palace to urge the emperor toward Shu.

sentences.zh: 甲午，百官朝者什無一二。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, of the hundred officials scarcely one or two in ten attended court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day scarcely one official in ten came to court.

sentences.zh: 上御勤政樓，下制，雲欲親征，聞者皆莫之信。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the Qinzheng Tower and issued an edict saying he would personally take the field; those who heard it none believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the Qinzheng Tower and issued an edict claiming he would take the field in person. No one believed it.

sentences.zh: 以京兆尹魏方進為御史大夫兼置頓使；

translations.literal: He appointed Metropolitan Magistrate Wei Fangjin Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Commissioner for Rest Stops;
translations.idiomatic: He made Metropolitan Magistrate Wei Fangjin Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner for Rest Stops;

sentences.zh: 京兆少尹靈昌崔光遠為京兆尹，充西京留守；

translations.literal: Assistant Metropolitan Magistrate of Lingchang Cui Guangyuan as Metropolitan Magistrate, acting as Western Capital Regent;
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Metropolitan Magistrate Cui Guangyuan of Lingchang as Metropolitan Magistrate and Regent of the Western Capital;

sentences.zh: 將軍邊令誠掌宮闈管鑰。

translations.literal: General Bian Lingcheng to hold the keys of the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: General Bian Lingcheng to hold the palace keys.

sentences.zh: 托以劍南節度大使穎王□將赴鎮，令本道設儲偫。

translations.literal: On the pretext that Military Commissioner of Jiannan Prince of Ying [—] was about to proceed to his post, he ordered that circuit to prepare stores.
translations.idiomatic: On the pretext that Prince of Ying, military commissioner of Jiannan, was about to take up his post, he ordered that circuit to prepare supplies.

sentences.zh: 是日，上移仗北內。

translations.literal: That day the emperor moved his guard to the Northern Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor withdrew to the Northern Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 既夕，命龍武大將軍陳玄禮整比六軍，厚賜錢帛，選閒廄馬九百餘匹，外人皆莫之知。

translations.literal: At evening he ordered Longwu Grand General Chen Xuanli to muster the Six Armies, gave generous gifts of money and silk, and selected more than nine hundred horses from the spare stables—outsiders knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he ordered Longwu Grand General Chen Xuanli to muster the Six Armies, gave lavish gifts of money and silk, and picked more than nine hundred horses from the spare stables. Outsiders knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 乙未，黎明，上獨與貴妃姊妹、皇子、妃、主、皇孫、楊國忠、韋見素、魏方進、陳玄禮及親近宦官、宮人出延秋門，妃、主、皇孫之在外者，皆委之而去。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, at dawn, the emperor alone with the Noble Consort and her sisters, princes, consorts, princesses, imperial grandsons, Yang Guozhong, Wei Jiansu, Wei Fangjin, Chen Xuanli, and close eunuchs and palace women went out the Yanqiu Gate; consorts, princesses, and grandsons who were outside were all abandoned and left behind.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on yiwei day the emperor slipped out the Yanqiu Gate with only the Noble Consort and her sisters, the princes, consorts, princesses, imperial grandsons, Yang Guozhong, Wei Jiansu, Wei Fangjin, Chen Xuanli, and a handful of close eunuchs and palace women. Consorts, princesses, and grandsons who were elsewhere were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 上過左藏，楊國忠請焚之，曰：「無為賊守。」

translations.literal: Passing the Left Treasury, Yang Guozhong asked to burn it, saying, "Do not leave it for the rebels to hold."
translations.idiomatic: Passing the Left Treasury, Yang Guozhong asked to burn it. "Do not leave it for the rebels," he said.

sentences.zh: 上愀然曰：「賊來不得，必更斂於百姓；

translations.literal: The emperor said somberly, "If the rebels cannot get it, they will surely levy it again from the common people;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said somberly, "If the rebels cannot take it, they will squeeze it from the people instead;

sentences.zh: 不如與之，無重困吾赤子。」

translations.literal: better to leave it for them and not doubly afflict our children."
translations.idiomatic: better leave it and not burden our people twice."

sentences.zh: 是日，百官猶有入朝者，至宮門，猶聞漏聲，三衛立仗儼然。

translations.literal: That day some officials still came to court; reaching the palace gates they still heard the water-clock and the Three Guards standing formation as usual.
translations.idiomatic: That day some officials still came to court. At the palace gates they still heard the water-clock and saw the Three Guards standing formation as if all were normal.

sentences.zh: 門既啟，則宮人亂出，中外擾攘，不知上所之。

translations.literal: Once the gates opened, palace women poured out in disorder; inside and outside were in turmoil, and no one knew where the emperor had gone.
translations.idiomatic: When the gates opened, palace women poured out in disorder. Inside and outside were chaos, and no one knew where the emperor had gone.

sentences.zh: 於是王公、士民四出逃竄，山谷細民爭入宮禁及王公第捨，盜取金寶，或乘驢上殿。

translations.literal: Thereupon nobles and commoners fled in all directions; humble folk from valleys and hills scrambled into the palace and noble mansions, stole gold and jewels, and some rode donkeys up into the halls.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and commoners fled in every direction. Humble folk from the hills stormed the palace and noble mansions, looted gold and jewels, and some rode donkeys into the halls.

sentences.zh: 又焚左藏大盈庫。

translations.literal: They also set fire to the Left Treasury and the Great Abundance Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: They also burned the Left Treasury and the Great Abundance Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 崔光遠、邊令誠帥人救火，又募人攝府、縣官分守之，殺十餘人，乃稍定。

translations.literal: Cui Guangyuan and Bian Lingcheng led men to fight the fire, also recruited men to act as prefectural and county officials to guard in sections, killed more than ten men, and only then was it somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guangyuan and Bian Lingcheng led men to fight the blaze, recruited stand-in prefectural and county officials to hold posts, killed more than ten looters, and only then brought some order.

sentences.zh: 光遠遣其子東見祿山，令誠亦以管鑰獻之。

translations.literal: Guangyuan sent his son Dong to see Lushan; Lingcheng also presented the keys.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan sent his son Dong to Lushan; Lingcheng presented the palace keys as well.

sentences.zh: 上過便橋，楊國忠使人焚橋。

translations.literal: The emperor passed Bian Bridge; Yang Guozhong had men burn the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian Bridge Yang Guozhong had the bridge burned behind them.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「士庶各避賊求生，奈何絕其路！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Soldiers and commoners alike flee the rebels to save their lives—how can we cut off their path!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Soldiers and townspeople alike flee the rebels to save their lives—how can we cut off their escape!"

sentences.zh: 留內侍監高力士，使撲滅乃來。

translations.literal: He left Inner Attendant Gao Lishi to have it extinguished and then come on.
translations.idiomatic: He left Inner Attendant Gao Lishi to put out the fire and then follow.

sentences.zh: 上遣宦者王洛卿前行，告諭郡縣置頓。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the eunuch Wang Luoqing ahead to announce to commanderies and counties to prepare rest stops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Wang Luoqing ahead to order the counties to prepare rest stops.

sentences.zh: 食時，至咸陽望賢宮，洛卿與縣令俱逃，中使徵召，吏民莫有應者。

translations.literal: At mealtime they reached Wangxian Palace at Xianyang; Luoqing and the county magistrate had both fled; palace envoys summoned, but no officials or people responded.
translations.idiomatic: At mealtime they reached Wangxian Palace at Xianyang. Luoqing and the county magistrate had both fled. Palace envoys called out, but no official or townsman answered.

sentences.zh: 日向中，上猶未食，楊國忠自市胡餅以獻。

translations.literal: The sun neared noon and the emperor had still not eaten; Yang Guozhong himself bought foreign cakes at market and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: The sun neared noon and the emperor had still not eaten. Yang Guozhong bought flatbread at market and offered them himself.

sentences.zh: 於是民爭獻糲飯，雜以麥豆；

translations.literal: Thereupon the people vied to offer coarse rice mixed with wheat and beans;
translations.idiomatic: Then the people pressed forward with coarse rice mixed with wheat and beans;

sentences.zh: 皇孫輩爭以手掬食之，須臾而盡，猶未能飽。

translations.literal: the imperial grandsons scrambled to scoop it up with their hands; in a moment it was gone and they were still not full.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial grandsons scooped it up in their hands; in a moment it was gone and they were still hungry.

sentences.zh: 上皆酬其直，慰勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor paid them all the fair price and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid them all fairly and spoke words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 眾皆哭，上亦掩泣。

translations.literal: All wept, and the emperor too covered his face and wept.
translations.idiomatic: All wept, and the emperor covered his face and wept as well.

sentences.zh: 有老父郭從謹進言曰：「祿山包藏禍心，固非一日；

translations.literal: An old man, Guo Congjin, came forward and said, "Lushan harbored evil intent—this was not a matter of a single day;
translations.idiomatic: An old man named Guo Congjin came forward: "Lushan harbored treason—this was no sudden thing;

sentences.zh: 亦有詣闕告其謀者，陛下往往誅之，使得逞其奸逆，致陛下播越。

translations.literal: there were also those who came to the court to report his plots, yet Your Majesty often executed them, allowing him to carry out his treachery and bringing Your Majesty to this exile.
translations.idiomatic: men came to court to report his plots, yet Your Majesty often had them killed, letting him carry out his treason and bringing Your Majesty to this exile.

sentences.zh: 是以先王務延訪忠良以廣聰明，蓋為此也。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings made it their task to seek out the loyal and good to broaden their understanding—surely it was for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the former kings sought out loyal and worthy men to broaden their understanding—surely for this very reason.

sentences.zh: 臣猶記宋璟為相，數進直言，天下賴以安平。

translations.literal: Your servant still remembers when Song Jing was chief minister—he repeatedly offered blunt counsel, and the empire relied on him for peace.
translations.idiomatic: I still remember when Song Jing was chief minister—he spoke blunt truth again and again, and the empire knew peace through him.

sentences.zh: 自頃以來，在廷之臣以言為諱，惟阿諛取容，是以闕門之外，陛下皆不得而知。

translations.literal: In recent times ministers at court have treated speech as taboo and only flattered to win favor, so beyond the palace gates Your Majesty has known nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years court ministers have treated speech as dangerous and flattered only to please, so beyond the palace gates Your Majesty has known nothing of the realm.

sentences.zh: 草野之臣，必知有今日久矣，但九重嚴邃，區區之心，無路上達。

translations.literal: Humble subjects in the wilds must have known this day would come long ago, but the Ninefold Gates are stern and deep—a petty heart had no road to reach upward.
translations.idiomatic: Men in the wilds must have foreseen this day long ago, but the Ninefold Gates are stern and deep—a humble heart had no road upward.

sentences.zh: 事不至此，臣何由得睹陛下之面而訴之乎！」

translations.literal: Had matters not come to this, how could your servant have beheld Your Majesty's face to speak thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Had matters not come to this, how could I ever have looked upon Your Majesty's face to speak thus!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此朕之不明，悔無所及！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is my own lack of clarity—regret comes too late!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is my own blindness—regret comes too late!"

sentences.zh: 慰諭而遣之。

translations.literal: He comforted him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 俄而尚食舉御膳以至，上命先賜從官，然後食之。

translations.literal: Before long the Imperial Kitchen brought the imperial meal; the emperor ordered it given first to the attending officials, then ate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Imperial Kitchen brought the imperial meal. The emperor had it served first to his attendants, then ate.

sentences.zh: 命軍士散詣村落求食，期未時皆集而行。

translations.literal: He ordered the soldiers to scatter to villages to seek food, with orders to assemble and march by the wei hour.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the soldiers to scatter into the villages for food, with orders to assemble and march by mid-afternoon.

sentences.zh: 夜將半，乃至金城。

translations.literal: Near midnight they reached Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Near midnight they reached Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 縣令亦逃，縣民皆脫身走，飲食器皿具在，士卒得以自給。

translations.literal: The magistrate had fled too; the county people had all slipped away, but food, drink, and vessels were all there, and the soldiers were able to supply themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate had fled and the townspeople had all slipped away, but food, drink, and vessels remained, and the soldiers helped themselves.

sentences.zh: 時從者多逃，內侍監袁思藝亦亡去，驛中無燈，人相枕藉而寢，貴賤無以復分辨。

translations.literal: Many of those in attendance had fled by then; Inner Attendant Yuan Siyi had also absconded; there were no lamps in the post station; people slept piled one upon another, and high and low could no longer be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Many attendants had fled by then; Inner Attendant Yuan Siyi had absconded as well. There were no lamps in the post station. Men slept piled atop one another, and noble and common could no longer be told apart.

sentences.zh: 王思禮自潼關至，始知哥舒翰被擒；

translations.literal: Wang Silun came from Tong Pass and only then learned Geshu Han had been captured;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Silun came from Tong Pass with word that Geshu Han had been captured;

sentences.zh: 以思禮為河西、隴右節度使，即令赴鎮，收合散卒，以俟東討。

translations.literal: Silun was appointed Military Commissioner of Hexi and Longyou and at once ordered to proceed to his post, gather scattered troops, and await the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Silun was made Military Commissioner of Hexi and Longyou and ordered at once to his post to gather scattered troops for the eastern campaign to come.

sentences.zh: 丙申，至馬嵬驛，將士饑疲，皆憤怒。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen they reached Mawei Post Station; the officers and soldiers, hungry and weary, were all enraged.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day they reached Mawei Post Station. The officers and soldiers, hungry and exhausted, were furious.

sentences.zh: 陳玄禮以禍由楊國忠，欲誅之，因東宮宦者李輔國以告太子，太子未決。

translations.literal: Chen Xuanli, holding that the disaster sprang from Yang Guozhong, wished to execute him and through Eastern Palace eunuch Li Fuguo informed the Crown Prince; the Prince had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuanli blamed Yang Guozhong for the disaster and wished to kill him. Through Eastern Palace eunuch Li Fuguo he informed the Crown Prince, who had not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃使者二十餘人遮國忠馬，訴以無食，國忠未及對，軍士呼曰：「國忠與胡虜謀反！」

translations.literal: It happened that more than twenty Tibetan envoys blocked Guozhong's horse, complaining they had no food; before Guozhong could answer, the soldiers shouted, "Guozhong plots rebellion with the barbarians!"
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty Tibetan envoys blocked Guozhong's horse, complaining they had no food. Before Guozhong could answer, the soldiers shouted, "Guozhong plots rebellion with the barbarians!"

sentences.zh: 或射之，中鞍。

translations.literal: Some shot at him and struck his saddle.
translations.idiomatic: Some shot at him and struck his saddle.

sentences.zh: 國忠走至西門內，軍士追殺之，屠割支體，以槍揭其首於驛門外，並殺其子戶部侍郎暄及韓國、秦國夫人。

translations.literal: Guozhong fled to inside the west gate; the soldiers pursued and killed him, hacked apart his limbs, and impaled his head on a spear outside the post gate; they also killed his son, Vice Minister of Revenue Xuan, and the Ladies of Han and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong fled inside the west gate. The soldiers pursued and killed him, hacked his body apart, and impaled his head on a spear outside the post gate. They also killed his son Xuan, Vice Minister of Revenue, and the Ladies of Han and Qin.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫魏方進曰：「汝曹何敢害宰相！」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin said, "How dare you harm the chief minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin cried, "How dare you harm the chief minister!"

sentences.zh: 眾又殺之。

translations.literal: The mob killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: The mob killed him too.

sentences.zh: 韋見素聞亂而出，為亂兵所撾，腦血流地。

translations.literal: Wei Jiansu, hearing the turmoil, came out and was beaten by the rioting soldiers until blood flowed from his head upon the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiansu, hearing the uproar, came out and was beaten by the mob until blood streamed from his head upon the ground.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「勿傷韋相公。」

translations.literal: The crowd said, "Do not harm Chancellor Wei."
translations.idiomatic: The crowd cried, "Do not harm Chancellor Wei."

sentences.zh: 救之，得免。

translations.literal: They rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: They pulled him back and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 軍士圍驛，上聞喧嘩，問外何事，左右以國忠反對。

translations.literal: The soldiers surrounded the post station; the emperor heard the clamor and asked what was happening outside; his attendants answered that Guozhong had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers surrounded the post station. The emperor heard the uproar and asked what was happening outside. His attendants said Guozhong had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 上杖屨出驛門，慰勞軍士，令收隊，軍士不應。

translations.literal: The emperor came out the post gate leaning on his staff and slippers, comforted the soldiers, and ordered them to fall in; they would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came out the post gate leaning on staff and slippers, spoke words of comfort, and ordered them to fall in. They would not obey.

sentences.zh: 上使高力士問之，玄禮對曰：「國忠謀反，貴妃不宜供奉，願陛下割恩正法。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Gao Lishi to ask; Xuanli replied, "Guozhong plotted rebellion; the Noble Consort should not remain in attendance—Your Majesty, we beg you cut affection and apply the law."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Gao Lishi to ask. Xuanli replied, "Guozhong plotted rebellion. The Noble Consort must not remain in attendance. We beg Your Majesty cut affection and apply the law."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕當自處之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I shall handle it myself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I shall handle it myself."

sentences.zh: 入門，倚杖傾首而立。

translations.literal: He entered the gate, leaned on his staff with head bowed, and stood.
translations.idiomatic: He went inside, leaned on his staff with head bowed, and stood in silence.

sentences.zh: 久之，京兆司錄韋諤前言曰：「今眾怒難犯，安危在晷刻，願陛下速決！」

translations.literal: After a long while, Metropolitan Recorder Wei E came forward and said, "Now the people's wrath cannot be defied; safety and peril hang on the turning of a shadow—Your Majesty, we beg you decide swiftly!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Metropolitan Recorder Wei E came forward: "The people's wrath cannot be defied. Safety and peril hang on the turning of a shadow. We beg Your Majesty decide at once!"

sentences.zh: 因叩頭流血。

translations.literal: He thereupon knocked his head until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: He knocked his head upon the ground until blood flowed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「貴妃常居深宮，安知國忠反謀！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The Noble Consort always dwelt deep in the palace—how could she know Guozhong's treasonous plot!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Noble Consort always dwelt deep in the palace—how could she know of Guozhong's treason!"

sentences.zh: 高力士曰：「貴妃誠無罪，然將士已殺國忠，而貴妃在陛下左右，豈敢自安！

translations.literal: Gao Lishi said, "The Noble Consort is indeed without guilt, yet the soldiers have already killed Guozhong, and with the Noble Consort at Your Majesty's side, how dare they feel secure!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi said, "The Noble Consort is indeed without guilt, yet the soldiers have killed Guozhong. With the Noble Consort at Your Majesty's side, how can they feel secure!

sentences.zh: 願陛下審思之，將士安，則陛下安矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, consider carefully—if the soldiers are secure, then Your Majesty is secure."
translations.idiomatic: Consider carefully, Your Majesty—if the soldiers are secure, then Your Majesty is secure."

sentences.zh: 上乃命力士引貴妃於佛堂，縊殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered Lishi to lead the Noble Consort to the Buddha hall and strangle her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Lishi to lead the Noble Consort to the Buddha hall and strangle her.

sentences.zh: 輿屍置驛庭，召玄禮等入視之。

translations.literal: Her body was carried out and placed in the post courtyard; Xuanli and the others were summoned in to view it.
translations.idiomatic: Her body was carried into the post courtyard. Xuanli and the others were summoned to view it.

sentences.zh: 玄禮等乃免冑釋甲，頓首請罪，上慰勞之，令曉諭軍士。

translations.literal: Xuanli and the others then removed helmets and armor, knocked their heads in confession of guilt; the emperor comforted them and ordered them to announce this to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanli and the others removed helmets and armor and knocked their heads in confession. The emperor comforted them and ordered them to announce this to the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 玄禮等呼萬歲，再拜而出，於是始整部伍為行計。

translations.literal: Xuanli and the others shouted "Long live the emperor!" bowed twice, and withdrew; only then did they begin to reorganize the ranks for the march.
translations.idiomatic: They shouted "Long live the emperor!" bowed twice, and withdrew. Only then did they begin to reorganize the ranks for the march.

sentences.zh: 諤，見素之子也。

translations.literal: E was Jiansu's son.
translations.idiomatic: E was Jiansu's son.

sentences.zh: 國忠妻裴柔與其幼子晞及虢國夫人、夫人子裴徽皆走，至陳倉，縣令薛景仙帥吏士追捕，誅之。

translations.literal: Guozhong's wife Pei Rou and his young son Xi, together with the Lady of Guo and the Lady's son Pei Hui, all fled; reaching Chencang, Magistrate Xue Jingxian led officials and soldiers in pursuit and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's wife Pei Rou, his young son Xi, the Lady of Guo, and her son Pei Hui all fled. At Chencang Magistrate Xue Jingxian led officials and soldiers in pursuit and executed them.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，上將發馬嵬，朝臣惟韋見素一人，乃以韋諤為御史中丞，充置頓使。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou the emperor was about to depart Mawei; of court ministers only Wei Jiansu remained, and Wei E was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner for Rest Stops.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the emperor was about to leave Mawei. Of court ministers only Wei Jiansu remained. Wei E was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner for Rest Stops.

sentences.zh: 將士皆曰：「國忠謀反，其將吏皆在蜀，不可往。」

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers all said, "Guozhong plotted rebellion; his commanders and officials are all in Shu—we cannot go there."
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers all said, "Guozhong plotted rebellion. His commanders and officials are all in Shu—we cannot go there."

sentences.zh: 或請之河、隴，或請之靈武，或請之太原，或言還京師。

translations.literal: Some urged going to He and Long, some to Lingwu, some to Taiyuan, and some spoke of returning to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged He and Long, some Lingwu, some Taiyuan, and some spoke of returning to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上意在入蜀，慮違眾心，竟不言所向。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was set on entering Shu, but fearing to go against the people's will, he finally said nothing of where he was headed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was set on Shu, but fearing to defy the army's will, he said nothing of where he was headed.

sentences.zh: 韋諤曰：「還京，當有御賊之備。

translations.literal: Wei E said, "If we return to the capital, we must have preparations against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wei E said, "If we return to the capital, we must have preparations against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 今兵少，未易東向，不如且至扶風，徐圖去就。」

translations.literal: Now our troops are few and it is not easy to turn east; better to go first to Fufeng and slowly consider where to go."
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are few and we cannot easily turn east. Better go first to Fufeng and consider our course slowly."

sentences.zh: 上詢於眾，眾以為然，乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the crowd, and all thought it right, so they followed this plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the crowd, and all agreed, so they followed this plan.

sentences.zh: 及行，父老皆遮道請留，曰：「宮闕，陛下家居，陵寢，陛下墳墓，今捨此，欲何之？」

translations.literal: As they marched, elders blocked the road begging them to stay, saying, "The palace is Your Majesty's home; the tombs are Your Majesty's graves—now you abandon these; where do you wish to go?"
translations.idiomatic: As they marched, elders blocked the road begging them to stay: "The palace is Your Majesty's home; the tombs are Your Majesty's graves. Now you abandon these—where do you mean to go?"

sentences.zh: 上為之按轡久之，乃命太子於後宣慰父老。

translations.literal: The emperor reined in his horse for them a long while, then ordered the Crown Prince to follow behind and comfort the elders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reined in his horse a long while, then ordered the Crown Prince to follow behind and comfort the elders.

sentences.zh: 父老因曰：「至尊既不肯留，某等願帥子弟從殿下東破賊，取長安。

translations.literal: The elders thereupon said, "Since Your Majesty will not stay, we wish to lead our sons and younger brothers to follow Your Highness east, break the rebels, and recover Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The elders then said, "Since Your Majesty will not stay, we wish to lead our sons and younger brothers to follow Your Highness east, break the rebels, and recover Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 若殿下與至尊皆入蜀，使中原百姓誰為之主？」

translations.literal: If Your Highness and Your Majesty both enter Shu, who will be master for the common people of the central plains?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness and Your Majesty both enter Shu, who will be master for the people of the central plains?"

sentences.zh: 須臾，眾至數千人。

translations.literal: In a moment the crowd reached several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the crowd swelled to several thousand.

sentences.zh: 太子不可，曰：「至尊遠冒險阻，吾豈忍朝夕離左右。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince would not agree and said, "Your Majesty ventures far through peril—I cannot bear to leave your side morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince refused: "Your Majesty ventures far through peril—I cannot bear to leave your side morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 且吾尚未面辭，當還白至尊，更稟進止。」

translations.literal: Moreover I have not yet taken leave in person—I should return to report to Your Majesty and receive further orders."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have not yet taken leave in person. I must return to report to Your Majesty and receive further orders."

sentences.zh: 涕泣，跋馬欲西。

translations.literal: Weeping, he spurred his horse intending to go west.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he spurred his horse to go west.

sentences.zh: 建寧王倓與李輔國執鞚諫曰：「逆胡犯闕，四海分崩，不因人情，何以興復！

translations.literal: Prince of Jianning Li Tan and Li Fuguo seized the reins and remonstrated, saying, "The rebel barbarians violate the capital and the four seas are sundered—without following the people's will, how can restoration be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jianning Li Tan and Li Fuguo seized the reins and remonstrated: "The rebels have seized the capital and the realm is sundered. Without following the people's will, how can we restore the dynasty!

sentences.zh: 今殿下從至尊入蜀，若賊兵燒絕棧道，則中原之地拱手授賊矣。

translations.literal: If Your Highness now follows Your Majesty into Shu and rebel troops burn and cut the plank roads, the lands of the central plains will be handed to the rebels with folded arms.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness follows Your Majesty into Shu and the rebels burn the plank roads, the central plains will be handed to the enemy without a fight.

sentences.zh: 人情既離，不可復合，雖欲復至此，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Once the people's hearts are lost they cannot be reunited; even if you wished to return to this moment, could you obtain it!
translations.idiomatic: Once the people's hearts are lost they cannot be won back. Even if you wished to return to this moment, could you?

sentences.zh: 不如收西北守邊之兵，召郭、李於河北，與之並力東討逆賊，克復二京，削平四海，使社稷危而復安，宗廟毀而更存，掃除宮禁以迎至尊，豈非孝之大者乎！

translations.literal: Better to gather the border-guarding troops of the northwest, summon Guo and Li from Hebei, join forces with them in an eastern campaign against the rebels, recover the Two Capitals, pacify the four seas, make the altars of state perilous yet restored and the ancestral temples ruined yet preserved, sweep clean the palace precincts to welcome Your Majesty—is this not the greatest filial piety!
translations.idiomatic: Better gather the northwest border troops, summon Guo and Li from Hebei, and join them in an eastern campaign to recover the Two Capitals and pacify the realm—restore the altars of state and the ancestral temples, sweep the palace clean to welcome Your Majesty. Is this not the greatest filial piety!

sentences.zh: 何必區區溫情，為兒女之戀乎！」

translations.literal: Why cling to petty tender feeling and the love of sons and daughters!"
translations.idiomatic: Why cling to petty tenderness and the love of sons and daughters!"

sentences.zh: 廣平王俶亦勸太子留。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangping Li Chu also urged the Crown Prince to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangping Li Chu also urged the Crown Prince to remain.

sentences.zh: 父老共擁太子馬，不得行。

translations.literal: The elders together seized the Crown Prince's horse so he could not go.
translations.idiomatic: The elders together seized the Crown Prince's horse so he could not leave.

sentences.zh: 太子乃使俶馳白上。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince thereupon sent Chu riding swiftly to report to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince sent Chu riding swiftly to report to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上總轡待太子，久不至，使人偵之，還白狀，上曰：「天也！」

translations.literal: The emperor gathered his reins and waited for the Crown Prince; long he did not come; he sent men to spy out the situation; they returned and reported; the emperor said, "Heaven's will!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reined in his horse and waited for the Crown Prince. When he did not come for a long while, the emperor sent men to learn what had happened. They returned and reported. The emperor said, "Heaven's will!"

sentences.zh: 乃命分後軍二千人及飛龍廄馬從太子，且諭將士曰：「太子仁孝，可奉宗廟，汝曹善輔佐之。」

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered two thousand men from the rear guard and Flying Dragon Stud horses given to follow the Crown Prince, and also instructed the soldiers, "The Crown Prince is benevolent and filial and can uphold the ancestral temples—you must assist him well."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered two thousand men from the rear guard and Flying Dragon Stud horses to follow the Crown Prince, and told the soldiers: "The Crown Prince is benevolent and filial and can uphold the ancestral temples. Assist him well."

sentences.zh: 又諭太子曰：「汝勉之，勿以吾為念。

translations.literal: He also instructed the Crown Prince, "Strive on—do not think of me.
translations.idiomatic: He also told the Crown Prince: "Strive on—do not think of me.

sentences.zh: 西北諸胡，吾撫之素厚，汝必得其用。」

translations.literal: The various barbarians of the northwest—I have always treated them generously; you will surely win their service."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians of the northwest—I have always treated them generously. You will surely win their service."

sentences.zh: 太子南向號泣而已。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince faced south and wept aloud, and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince faced south and wept aloud, and that was all.

sentences.zh: 又使送東宮內人於太子，且宣旨欲傳位，太子不受。

translations.literal: He also had Eastern Palace women sent to the Crown Prince and proclaimed his intent to abdicate; the Crown Prince would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Eastern Palace women to the Crown Prince and proclaimed his intent to abdicate. The Crown Prince refused.

sentences.zh: 俶、倓，皆太子之子也。

translations.literal: Chu and Tan were both sons of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Tan were both sons of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 己亥，上至岐山。

translations.literal: On the day jihai the emperor reached Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day the emperor reached Qishan.

sentences.zh: 或言賊前鋒且至，上遽過，宿扶風郡。

translations.literal: Someone said the rebel vanguard was about to arrive; the emperor hurried past and lodged at Fufeng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that the rebel vanguard was near. The emperor hurried on and lodged at Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 士卒潛懷去就，往往流言不遜，陳玄禮不能制，上患之。

translations.literal: The soldiers secretly weighed staying or leaving; often seditious rumors spread; Chen Xuanli could not control them, and the emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers secretly weighed desertion. Seditious rumors spread. Chen Xuanli could not control them, and the emperor was troubled.

sentences.zh: 會成都貢春彩十餘萬匹，至扶風，上命悉陳之於庭，召將士入，臨軒諭之曰：「朕比來衰耄，托任失人，致逆胡亂常，須遠避其鋒。

translations.literal: It happened that Chengdu's tribute of more than a hundred thousand bolts of spring silk arrived at Fufeng; the emperor ordered it all displayed in the courtyard, summoned the officers and soldiers in, and from the hall addressed them, saying, "I of late have grown old and feeble, entrusted office to the wrong men, and brought the rebel barbarians to disorder the norms—I must flee far from their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu's tribute of more than a hundred thousand bolts of spring silk arrived at Fufeng. The emperor had it displayed in the courtyard, summoned the officers and soldiers, and from the hall addressed them: "I have grown old and feeble, entrusted office to the wrong men, and brought the rebels to disorder the realm. I must flee far from their edge.

sentences.zh: 知卿等皆蒼猝從朕，不得別父母妻子，茇涉至此，勞苦至矣，朕甚愧之。

translations.literal: I know you all followed me in haste, unable to bid farewell to parents, wives, and children, and have trudged here through hardship to the utmost—I am deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: I know you all followed me in haste, unable to bid farewell to parents, wives, and children, and have trudged here through the utmost hardship. I am deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 蜀路阻長，郡縣褊小，人馬眾多，或不能供，今聽卿等各還家，朕獨與子、孫、中官前行入蜀，亦足自達。

translations.literal: The road to Shu is long and obstructed, the commanderies and counties narrow and small—with so many men and horses, perhaps they cannot supply us. Now I permit you each to return home; I alone with sons, grandsons, and palace eunuchs will go forward into Shu—that too will suffice to reach it.
translations.idiomatic: The road to Shu is long and difficult, the counties small—with so many men and horses they may not be able to supply us. I permit you each to return home. I alone with sons, grandsons, and palace eunuchs will go on into Shu—that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 今日與卿等訣別，可共分此彩，以備資糧。

translations.literal: Today I take leave of you—divide this silk among yourselves for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Today I take leave of you. Divide this silk among yourselves for provisions.

sentences.zh: 若歸，見父母及長安父老，為朕致意，各好自愛也！」

translations.literal: If you return and see your parents and the elders of Chang'an, convey my regards and tell them each to take good care!"
translations.idiomatic: If you return and see your parents and the elders of Chang'an, convey my regards and tell them to take good care!"

sentences.zh: 因泣下沾襟。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept until his robe was soaked.
translations.idiomatic: He wept until his robe was soaked.

sentences.zh: 眾皆哭，曰：「臣等死生從陛下，不敢有貳。」

translations.literal: All wept and said, "Your servants live and die with Your Majesty and dare not be of two minds."
translations.idiomatic: All wept and said, "We live and die with Your Majesty and dare not desert you."

sentences.zh: 上良久曰：「去留聽卿。」

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor said, "Stay or go—as you wish."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the emperor said, "Stay or go—as you wish."

sentences.zh: 自是流言始息。

translations.literal: From then on the seditious rumors began to cease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the seditious rumors ceased.

sentences.zh: 太子既留，未知所適。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince having stayed behind, he did not yet know where to go.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince had stayed behind but did not yet know where to go.

sentences.zh: 廣平王俶曰：「日漸晏，此不可駐，眾欲何之？」

translations.literal: Prince of Guangping Chu said, "The day grows late—this place cannot be held. Where does the crowd wish to go?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangping Chu said, "The day grows late—this place cannot be held. Where does everyone wish to go?"

sentences.zh: 皆莫對。

translations.literal: None answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 建寧王倓曰：「殿下昔嘗為朔方節度大使，將吏歲時致啟，倓略識其姓名。

translations.literal: Prince of Jianning Tan said, "Your Highness once served as Military Commissioner of Shuofang; the officers sent seasonal greetings each year—I roughly know their names.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jianning Tan said, "Your Highness once served as Military Commissioner of Shuofang. The officers sent seasonal greetings each year—I roughly know their names.

sentences.zh: 今河西、隴右之眾皆敗降賊，父兄子弟多在賊中，或生異圖。

translations.literal: Now the troops of Hexi and Longyou have mostly been defeated and surrendered to the rebels; fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers are mostly among the rebels—some may harbor other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Now the troops of Hexi and Longyou have mostly been defeated and surrendered. Their kin are mostly among the rebels—some may harbor other designs.

sentences.zh: 朔方道近，士馬全盛，裴冕衣冠名族，必無貳心。

translations.literal: The Shuofang circuit is near, its soldiers and horses in full strength; Pei Mian is of a great robe-and-cap clan and will surely have no second heart.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang is near, its soldiers and horses in full strength. Pei Mian is of a great official clan and will surely prove loyal.

sentences.zh: 賊入長安方虜掠，未暇徇地，乘此速往就之，徐圖大舉，此上策也。

translations.literal: The rebels have just entered Chang'an and are still plundering, with no leisure to extend control over the land—seize this moment to go swiftly thither, then slowly plan a great campaign. This is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels have just entered Chang'an and are still plundering, with no leisure to extend control. Seize this moment, go swiftly thither, and plan a great campaign. This is the best course.

sentences.zh: 眾皆曰：「善！」

translations.literal: All said, "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Good!"

sentences.zh: 至渭濱，遇潼關敗卒，誤與之戰，死傷甚衆。

translations.literal: Reaching the Wei bank, they met defeated troops from Tong Pass and mistakenly fought them, with very many killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the Wei bank, they met defeated troops from Tong Pass and mistakenly fought them, with heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 已，乃收餘卒，擇渭水淺處，乘馬涉渡；

translations.literal: Afterward they gathered the survivors, chose a shallow place on the Wei, and crossed on horseback;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they gathered the survivors, found a shallow place on the Wei, and crossed on horseback;

sentences.zh: 無馬者涕泣而返。

translations.literal: those without horses wept and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: those without horses wept and turned back.

sentences.zh: 太子自奉天北上，比至新平，通夜馳三百餘里，士卒、器械失亡過半，所存之眾不過數百。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince from Fengtian marched north; by the time he reached Xinping he had ridden more than three hundred li through the night; soldiers and equipment lost were more than half—the force remaining was no more than several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince marched north from Fengtian. By Xinping he had ridden more than three hundred li through the night. More than half his men and equipment were lost—the force remaining numbered only a few hundred.

sentences.zh: 新平太守薛羽棄郡走，太子斬之，是日，至安定，太守徐瑴亦走，又斬之。

translations.literal: Xinping Administrator Xue Yu abandoned the commandery and fled; the Crown Prince beheaded him. That day he reached Anding; Administrator Xu Jun also fled and was beheaded as well.
translations.idiomatic: Xinping Administrator Xue Yu abandoned his post and fled; the Crown Prince beheaded him. That day he reached Anding; Administrator Xu Jun also fled and was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以劍南節度留後崔圓為劍南節度等副大使。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Cui Yuan, acting commissioner of Jiannan, was appointed Vice Military Commissioner of Jiannan and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Cui Yuan, acting commissioner of Jiannan, was appointed Vice Military Commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，上發扶風，宿陳倉。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou the emperor departed Fufeng and lodged at Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the emperor left Fufeng and lodged at Chencang.

sentences.zh: 太子至烏氏，彭原太守李遵出迎，獻衣及糗糧。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince reached Wushi; Pengyuan Administrator Li Zun came out to welcome him and presented clothing and dry provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince reached Wushi. Pengyuan Administrator Li Zun came out to welcome him with clothing and dry provisions.

sentences.zh: 至彭原，募士，得數百人。

translations.literal: Reaching Pengyuan, he recruited soldiers and obtained several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengyuan he recruited soldiers and obtained several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 是日，至平涼，閱監牧馬，得數萬匹，又募士，得五百餘人，軍勢稍振。

translations.literal: That day he reached Pingliang, inspected the stud herds, and obtained tens of thousands of horses; he also recruited soldiers and obtained more than five hundred men; military strength was somewhat restored.
translations.idiomatic: That day he reached Pingliang, inspected the stud herds, and obtained tens of thousands of horses. He recruited more than five hundred soldiers. Military strength was somewhat restored.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，上至散關，分扈從將士為六軍，使穎王□先行詣劍南。

translations.literal: On the day renyin the emperor reached San Pass, divided the accompanying officers and soldiers into six armies, and sent Prince of Ying [—] ahead first to proceed to Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day the emperor reached San Pass, divided his escort into six armies, and sent Prince of Ying ahead first toward Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 壽王瑁等分將六軍以次之。

translations.literal: Prince of Shou Li Mao and others each commanded one of the six armies in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shou Li Mao and others each commanded one of the six armies in turn.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上至河池郡。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu the emperor reached Hechi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day the emperor reached Hechi.

sentences.zh: 崔圓奉表迎車駕，具陳蜀土豐稔，甲兵全盛。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan submitted a memorial welcoming the imperial carriage, fully describing Shu lands as abundant in harvest and arms and armor in full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan submitted a memorial welcoming the imperial carriage, describing Shu as abundant in harvest and fully armed.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，即日，以圓為中書侍郎、同平章事，蜀郡長史如故。
