translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; that same day Yuan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councillor, retaining his post as Chief Secretary of Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. That same day Yuan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councillor, retaining his post as Chief Secretary of Shu.

sentences.zh: 以隴西公瑀為漢中王、梁州都督、山南西道採訪防禦使。

translations.literal: Prince of Longxi Li Yu was made Prince of Hanzhong, Area Commander of Liangzhou, and Investigation and Defense Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Longxi Li Yu was made Prince of Hanzhong, Area Commander of Liangzhou, and Investigation and Defense Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 瑀，璡之弟也。

translations.literal: Yu was the younger brother of Li Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was the younger brother of Li Jin.

sentences.zh: 王思禮至平涼，聞河西諸胡亂，還，詣行在。

translations.literal: Wang Silun reached Pingliang, heard the various barbarians of Hexi were in turmoil, returned, and went to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Silun reached Pingliang, heard the barbarians of Hexi were in turmoil, and returned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 初，河西諸胡部落聞其都護皆從哥舒翰沒於潼關，故爭自立，相攻擊；

translations.literal: Initially, the tribal groups of Hexi heard their protectors had all perished with Geshu Han at Tong Pass and therefore vied to set themselves up independently and attacked one another;
translations.idiomatic: The tribal groups of Hexi had heard their protectors had all perished with Geshu Han at Tong Pass and vied to set themselves up independently, attacking one another;

sentences.zh: 而都護實從翰在北岸，不死，又不與火拔歸仁俱降賊。

translations.literal: yet the protector had in fact followed Han on the north bank and did not die, and did not surrender to the rebels together with Huoba Guiren.
translations.idiomatic: yet the protector had in fact followed Han on the north bank, did not die, and did not surrender with Huoba Guiren.

sentences.zh: 上乃以河西兵馬使周泌為河西節度使，隴右兵馬使彭元耀為隴右節度使，與都護思結進明等俱之鎮，招其部落。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon appointed Hexi Army-and-Horse Commissioner Zhou Bi Military Commissioner of Hexi, Longyou Army-and-Horse Commissioner Peng Yuanyao Military Commissioner of Longyou, and together with Protector Sinü Jinming and others proceeded to their posts to summon the tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Zhou Bi Military Commissioner of Hexi and Peng Yuanyao Military Commissioner of Longyou, and together with Protector Sinü Jinming and others proceeded to their posts to summon the tribes.

sentences.zh: 以思禮為行在都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Silun was made Mobile Court Commissioner General of Army and Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Silun was made Mobile Court Commissioner General of Army and Horse.

sentences.zh: 戊申，扶風民康景龍等自相帥擊賊所署宣慰使薛總，斬首二百餘級。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, the people of Fufeng, Kang Jinglong and others, on their own initiative led an attack on the Pacification Commissioner appointed by the rebels, Xue Zong, and beheaded more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day the people of Fufeng, led by Kang Jinglong and others on their own initiative, attacked rebel Pacification Commissioner Xue Zong and took more than two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，陳倉令薛景仙殺賊守將，克扶風而守之。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Chencang Magistrate Xue Jingxian killed the rebel garrison commander, captured Fufeng, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day Chencang Magistrate Xue Jingxian killed the rebel garrison commander, captured Fufeng, and held it.

sentences.zh: 安祿山不意上遽西幸，遣使止崔乾祐兵留潼關，凡十日，乃遣孫孝哲將兵入長安，以張通儒為西京留守，崔光遠為京兆尹；

translations.literal: An Lushan had not expected the emperor to flee west so swiftly; he sent envoys ordering Cui Qianyu's troops to remain at Tong Pass—for ten days in all—only then sent Sun Xiaozhe to lead troops into Chang'an, appointing Zhang Tongru Western Capital Regent and Cui Guangyuan Metropolitan Magistrate;
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan had not expected the emperor to flee west so swiftly. He kept Cui Qianyu's troops at Tong Pass for ten days, then sent Sun Xiaozhe into Chang'an, appointing Zhang Tongru Western Capital Regent and Cui Guangyuan Metropolitan Magistrate;

sentences.zh: 使安忠順將兵屯苑中，以鎮關中。

translations.literal: he had An Zhongshun lead troops to encamp in the park precincts to secure Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: he had An Zhongshun encamp in the park precincts to secure Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 孝哲為祿山所寵任，尤用事，常與嚴莊爭權；

translations.literal: Xiaozhe was favored and entrusted by Lushan, especially wielded power, and often contended for authority with Yan Zhuang;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhe was favored by Lushan, wielded great power, and often contended with Yan Zhuang;

sentences.zh: 祿山使監關中諸將，通儒等皆受制於孝哲。

translations.literal: Lushan had him supervise the generals of Guanzhong; Tongru and the others were all subject to Xiaozhe.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had him supervise the Guanzhong generals; Tongru and the others were all subject to Xiaozhe.

sentences.zh: 教哲豪侈，果於殺戮，賊黨畏之。

translations.literal: Xiaozhe was extravagant and ruthless in killing; the rebel party feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhe was extravagant and ruthless in killing; the rebels feared him.

sentences.zh: 祿山命搜捕百官、宦者、宮女等，每獲數百人，輒以兵衛送洛陽。

translations.literal: Lushan ordered the search and capture of hundred officials, eunuchs, palace women, and the like; whenever several hundred were seized, troops escorted them to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan ordered the capture of officials, eunuchs, palace women, and the like. Whenever several hundred were seized, troops escorted them to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 王、侯、將、相扈從車駕、家留長安者，誅及嬰孩。

translations.literal: Kings, marquises, generals, and chancellors who had followed the imperial carriage or left families in Chang'an were executed down to infants.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, marquises, generals, and chancellors who had followed the emperor or left families in Chang'an were executed down to infants.

sentences.zh: 陳希烈以晚節失恩，怨上，與張均、張垍等皆降於賊。

translations.literal: Chen Xilie, having lost favor in his later years, resented the emperor and together with Zhang Jun, Zhang Yi, and others all surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xilie, having lost favor in his later years, resented the emperor and surrendered with Zhang Jun, Zhang Yi, and others.

sentences.zh: 祿山以希烈、垍為相，自餘朝士皆授以官。

translations.literal: Lushan made Xilie and Yi chancellors; all the remaining court gentlemen were given offices.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan made Xilie and Yi chancellors and gave offices to the remaining court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 於是賊勢大熾，西脅汧、隴，南侵江、漢，北割河東之半。

translations.literal: Thereupon rebel strength blazed greatly—pressing west upon Qian and Long, invading south into the Yangzi and Han, and cutting off half of Hedong in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel strength now blazed—pressing west upon Qian and Long, invading south into the Yangzi and Han, and seizing half of Hedong in the north.

sentences.zh: 然賊將皆粗猛無遠略，既克長安，自以為得志，日夜縱酒，專以聲色寶賄為事，無復西出之意，故上得安行入蜀，太子北行亦無追迫之患。

translations.literal: Yet the rebel generals were all crude and fierce without far-reaching plans; having captured Chang'an they thought themselves triumphant, drank day and night, devoted themselves to music, women, treasure, and bribes, and had no further intent to march west—therefore the emperor could travel safely into Shu and the Crown Prince march north without fear of pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebel generals were crude and fierce without far-reaching plans. Having taken Chang'an they thought themselves triumphant, drank day and night, and devoted themselves to pleasure and plunder, with no further intent to march west. Thus the emperor could travel safely into Shu and the Crown Prince north without fear of pursuit.

sentences.zh: 李光弼圍博陵未下，聞潼關不守，解圍而南。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi besieged Boling but had not taken it; hearing Tong Pass was lost, he lifted the siege and marched south.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi besieged Boling but had not taken it. Hearing Tong Pass was lost, he lifted the siege and marched south.

sentences.zh: 史思明踵其後，光弼擊卻之，與郭子儀皆引兵入井陘，留常山太守王輔將景城、河間團練兵守常山。

translations.literal: Shi Siming followed close behind; Guangbi struck and drove him back; he and Guo Ziyi both led troops into Jingxing Pass, leaving Changshan Administrator Wang Fu with Jingcheng and Hejian militia to defend Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming followed close behind. Guangbi struck and drove him back. He and Guo Ziyi both led troops into Jingxing Pass, leaving Wang Fu with Jingcheng and Hejian militia to defend Changshan.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使劉正臣將襲范陽，未至，史思明引兵逆擊之，正臣大敗，棄妻子走，士卒死者七千餘人。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Pinglu Liu Zhengchen was about to strike Fanyang but had not arrived; Shi Siming led troops to meet and strike him; Zhengchen suffered a great defeat, abandoned wife and children and fled, and more than seven thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Pinglu Commissioner Liu Zhengchen was marching on Fanyang when Siming met and routed him. Zhengchen abandoned wife and children and fled. More than seven thousand of his men died.

sentences.zh: 初，顏真卿聞河北節度使李光弼出井陘，即斂軍還平原，以待光弼之命。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yan Zhenqing heard Military Commissioner of Hebei Li Guangbi was coming out through Jingxing Pass, he at once gathered his army and returned to Pingyuan to await Guangbi's orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhenqing heard Hebei Commissioner Li Guangbi was coming out through Jingxing Pass, he gathered his army and returned to Pingyuan to await orders.

sentences.zh: 聞郭、李西入井陘，真卿始復區處河北軍事。

translations.literal: When he heard Guo and Li had entered Jingxing Pass to the west, Zhenqing only then resumed organizing Hebei military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Guo and Li had withdrawn into Jingxing Pass, Zhenqing resumed organizing Hebei military affairs.

sentences.zh: 太子至平涼數日，朔方留後杜鴻漸、六城水陸運使魏少游、節度判官崔漪、支度判官盧簡金、鹽池判官李涵相與謀曰：「平涼散地，非屯兵之所，靈武兵食完富，若迎太子至此，北收諸城兵，西發河、隴勁騎，南向以定中原，此萬世一時也。」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince had been at Pingliang several days when Shuofang Acting Commissioner Du Hongjian, Six Cities Water-and-Land Transport Commissioner Wei Shaoyou, Circuit Judge Cui Yi, Supply Judge Lu Jianjin, and Salt Pond Judge Li Han deliberated together, saying, "Pingliang is open country—not a place to encamp troops. Lingwu's soldiers and provisions are complete and abundant. If we welcome the Crown Prince here, gather troops from the northern cities, send out the crack cavalry of He and Long to the west, and march south to settle the central plains—this is a once-in-ten-thousand-generations moment."
translations.idiomatic: After several days at Pingliang, Shuofang Acting Commissioner Du Hongjian, Transport Commissioner Wei Shaoyou, Circuit Judge Cui Yi, Supply Judge Lu Jianjin, and Salt Pond Judge Li Han deliberated: "Pingliang is open country—not a place to encamp. Lingwu's soldiers and provisions are abundant. Welcome the Crown Prince there, gather northern troops, send out He and Long cavalry, and march south to settle the central plains—this is a once-in-ten-thousand-generations chance."

sentences.zh: 乃使涵奉箋於太子，且籍朔方士馬、甲兵、谷帛、軍須之數以獻之。

translations.literal: They thereupon had Han present a memorial to the Crown Prince and also register and present the numbers of Shuofang's soldiers and horses, armor and weapons, grain and cloth, and military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: They had Han present a memorial to the Crown Prince and register Shuofang's soldiers, horses, arms, grain, cloth, and military supplies.

sentences.zh: 涵至平涼，太子大悅。

translations.literal: When Han reached Pingliang, the Crown Prince was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Han reached Pingliang, the Crown Prince was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 會河西司馬裴冕入為御史中丞，至平涼見太子，亦勸太子之朔方，太子從之。

translations.literal: It happened that Hexi Vice Commissioner Pei Mian had entered the capital as Vice Censor-in-Chief; reaching Pingliang he saw the Crown Prince and also urged him to go to Shuofang; the Crown Prince followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi Vice Commissioner Pei Mian had entered the capital as Vice Censor-in-Chief. Reaching Pingliang he urged the Crown Prince toward Shuofang, and the Crown Prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸，暹之族子；

translations.literal: Hongjian was a clansman of Du Huan;
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian was a clansman of Du Huan;

sentences.zh: 涵，道之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Han was the great-grandson of Li Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Han was the great-grandson of Li Dao.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸、漪使少游居後，葺次捨，庀資儲，自迎太子於平涼北境，說太子曰：「朔方，天下勁兵處也。

translations.literal: Hongjian and Yi had Shaoyou remain behind to repair lodgings and prepare stores, and themselves went to welcome the Crown Prince at Pingliang's northern border, saying to him, "Shuofang is where the empire's crack troops are stationed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian and Yi had Shaoyou remain behind to repair lodgings and prepare stores, and went themselves to welcome the Crown Prince at Pingliang's northern border: "Shuofang is where the empire's crack troops are stationed.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃請和，回紇內附，四方郡縣大抵堅守拒賊以俟興復。

translations.literal: Now Tibet seeks peace and the Uyghurs have submitted inward; commanderies and counties on all sides for the most part hold firm and resist the rebels awaiting restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet seeks peace and the Uyghurs have submitted. Commanderies and counties on all sides for the most part hold firm and resist the rebels, awaiting restoration.

sentences.zh: 殿下今理兵靈武，按轡長驅，移檄四方，收攬忠義，則逆賊不足屠也。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness now arrays troops at Lingwu, gathers the reins and drives far, sends proclamations to the four directions, and gathers the loyal and righteous, then the rebel traitors are not worth slaughtering."
translations.idiomatic: Array troops at Lingwu, gather the reins and drive far, send proclamations to the four directions, and gather the loyal—the rebel traitors will not stand."

sentences.zh: 少游盛治宮室，帷帳皆仿禁中，飲膳備水陸。

translations.literal: Shaoyou lavishly prepared palace chambers, with curtains and canopies all modeled on the inner palace, and provisions for feast and drink on land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou lavishly prepared palace chambers modeled on the inner palace, with provisions for feast and drink on land and water.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛酉，太子至靈武，悉命撤之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day xinyou, the Crown Prince reached Lingwu and ordered it all removed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinyou day, the Crown Prince reached Lingwu and ordered it all removed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上至普安，憲部侍郎房琯來謁見。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi the emperor reached Pu'an; Vice Minister of Justice Fang Guan came to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the emperor reached Pu'an. Vice Minister of Justice Fang Guan came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 上之發長安也，群臣多不知，至咸陽，謂高力士曰：「朝臣誰當來，誰不來？」

translations.literal: When the emperor departed Chang'an, most of the court did not know; reaching Xianyang he said to Gao Lishi, "Which court ministers will come and which will not?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor left Chang'an, most of the court did not know. At Xianyang he said to Gao Lishi, "Which court ministers will come and which will not?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「張均、張垍父子受陛下恩最深，且連戚裡，是必先來。

translations.literal: He answered, "Zhang Jun and Zhang Yi, father and son, have received Your Majesty's favor most deeply and are moreover connected by marriage—they will surely come first.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Zhang Jun and Zhang Yi have received Your Majesty's favor most deeply and are connected by marriage—they will surely come first.

sentences.zh: 時論皆謂房琯宜為相，而陛下不用，又祿山嘗薦之，恐或不來。」

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion all held Fang Guan fit to be chief minister, yet Your Majesty did not employ him; moreover Lushan once recommended him—I fear he may not come."
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held Fang Guan fit for chief minister, yet Your Majesty did not employ him. Lushan once recommended him—I fear he may not come."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「事未可知。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "That cannot yet be known."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That cannot yet be known."

sentences.zh: 及琯至，上問均兄弟，對曰：「臣帥與偕來，逗留不進：觀其意，似有所蓄而不能言也。」

translations.literal: When Guan arrived, the emperor asked about the Jun brothers; he answered, "Your servant's commander came with me but lingered without advancing—judging by their intent, they seem to harbor something they cannot speak."
translations.idiomatic: When Guan arrived, the emperor asked about the Jun brothers. Guan answered, "They came with me but lingered without advancing. Judging by their intent, they seem to harbor something they cannot speak."

sentences.zh: 上顧力士曰：「朕固知之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor looked at Lishi and said, "I knew it all along."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked at Lishi and said, "I knew it all along."

sentences.zh: 即日，以□為文部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: That same day, [Guan] was made Vice Minister of Culture and Fellow Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Guan was made Vice Minister of Culture and Fellow Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 初，張垍尚寧親公主，聽於禁中置宅，寵渥無比。

translations.literal: Initially, Zhang Yi married Princess Ningqin and was permitted to establish a residence within the forbidden precincts, favored beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi had married Princess Ningqin and was permitted a residence within the forbidden precincts, favored beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 陳希烈求解政務，上幸垍宅，問可為相者。

translations.literal: Chen Xilie requested release from administrative duties; the emperor visited Yi's residence and asked who could serve as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xilie requested release from office. The emperor visited Yi's residence and asked who could serve as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 垍未對。

translations.literal: Yi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi did not answer.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「無若愛婿。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "None like my beloved son-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "None like my beloved son-in-law."

sentences.zh: 垍降階拜舞。

translations.literal: Yi descended the steps and bowed in the dance of obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Yi descended the steps and bowed in obeisance.

sentences.zh: 既而不用，故垍懷怏怏，上亦覺之。

translations.literal: Yet afterward he was not employed, so Yi harbored resentment, and the emperor too perceived it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward he was not employed. Yi harbored resentment, and the emperor perceived it.

sentences.zh: 是時均、垍兄弟及姚崇之子尚書右丞奕、蕭蒿之子兵部侍郎華、韋安石之子禮部侍郎陟、太常少卿斌，皆以才望至大官，上嘗曰：「或命相，當遍舉故相子弟耳。」

translations.literal: At that time the Jun and Yi brothers, together with Yao Chong's son Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yi, Xiao Song's son Vice Minister of War Hua, Wei Anshi's sons Vice Minister of Rites Zhi and Vice Minister of Ceremonies Bin, all by talent and repute attained high office. The emperor once said, "When appointing a chief minister, one ought simply to recommend the sons and younger brothers of former chief ministers."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the brothers Zhang Jun and Zhang Yi, together with Yao Chong's son Yi (Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat), Xiao Song's son Hua (Vice Minister of War), and Wei Anshi's sons Zhi (Vice Minister of Rites) and Bin (Vice Minister of Ceremonies), had all risen to high office on talent and reputation. The emperor once said, "When it comes time to appoint a chief minister, one need only recommend the sons of former chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 既而皆不用。

translations.literal: Yet in the end none were employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, none of them were appointed.

sentences.zh: 裴冕、杜鴻漸等上太子箋，請遵馬嵬之命，即皇帝位，太子不許。

translations.literal: Pei Mian, Du Hongjian, and others submitted a memorial to the Crown Prince requesting that he follow the command given at Mawei and immediately ascend the imperial throne. The Crown Prince did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian, Du Hongjian, and others submitted a memorial to the Crown Prince asking him to follow the command issued at Mawei and take the throne at once. The Crown Prince refused.

sentences.zh: 冕等言曰：「將士皆關中人，日夜思歸，所以崎嶇從殿下遠涉沙塞者，冀尺寸之功。

translations.literal: Mian and the others spoke, saying, "The officers and soldiers are all men of Guanzhong; day and night they think of returning home. The reason they have followed Your Highness over rugged terrain deep into the desert frontier is to hope for even the smallest measure of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Mian and the others said, "The officers and soldiers are all from Guanzhong and long day and night to go home. They have followed Your Highness over hard roads deep into the frontier only in hopes of winning some small measure of merit.

sentences.zh: 若一朝離散，不可復集。

translations.literal: If they should disperse in a single morning, they cannot be gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: If they scatter overnight, they cannot be assembled again.

sentences.zh: 願殿下勉徇眾心，為社稷計！」

translations.literal: We hope Your Highness will earnestly yield to the will of the multitude and act for the sake of the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Highness to yield to the army's will for the sake of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 箋五上，太子乃許之。

translations.literal: After the memorial was submitted five times, the Crown Prince then consented.
translations.idiomatic: After five such memorials, the Crown Prince finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 是日，肅宗即位於靈武城南樓，群臣舞蹈，上流涕歔欷。

translations.literal: That day, Emperor Suzong took the throne at the south tower of Lingwu. The assembled ministers performed the ritual dance. The emperor wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: That day Emperor Suzong ascended the throne at the south tower of Lingwu. The ministers performed the court dance of submission while the new emperor wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 尊玄宗曰上皇天帝，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: He honored Emperor Xuanzong as Retired Emperor and Heavenly Sovereign, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Emperor Xuanzong as Retired Emperor and Heavenly Sovereign, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 以杜鴻漸、崔漪並知中書舍人事，裴冕為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: He appointed Du Hongjian and Cui Yi jointly to handle the affairs of Secretariat Drafting Officer; Pei Mian became Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hongjian and Cui Yi were both put in charge of Secretariat drafting affairs; Pei Mian was made Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 改關內採訪使為節度使，徒治安化，以前蒲關防禦使呂崇賁為之。

translations.literal: He changed the Guannei Investigation Commissioner to Military Commissioner and relocated the administration to Anhua commandery, appointing former Puguan Defense Commissioner Lü Chongben to the post.
translations.idiomatic: The Guannei Investigation Commissioner was redesignated a military commissioner, with administration relocated to Anhua commandery; former Puguan Defense Commissioner Lü Chongben was appointed to the post.

sentences.zh: 以陳倉令薛景仙為扶風太守，兼防禦使；

translations.literal: He made Chencang Magistrate Xue Jingxian Administrator of Fufeng, concurrently Defense Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Chencang Magistrate Xue Jingxian was made Administrator of Fufeng and concurrent Defense Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使郭英乂為天水太守，兼防禦使。

translations.literal: Longyou Military Commissioner Guo Yingyi was made Administrator of Tianshui, concurrently Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou Military Commissioner Guo Yingyi was made Administrator of Tianshui and concurrent Defense Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時塞上精兵皆選入討賊，惟餘老弱守邊，文武官不滿三十人，披草萊，立朝廷，制度草創，武人驕慢。

translations.literal: At that time the elite troops on the frontier had all been selected for the campaign against the rebels; only the old and weak remained to guard the border. Civil and military officials numbered fewer than thirty. They cleared grass and scrub to establish a court; institutions were rudimentary, and military men were arrogant and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier's best troops had all been drafted for the anti-rebel campaign, leaving only the aged and weak to hold the border. Fewer than thirty civil and military officials remained. They hacked clearings in the wild grass to set up a court, improvised institutions from scratch, and faced swaggering, insubordinate soldiers.

sentences.zh: 大將管崇嗣在朝堂，背闕而坐，言笑自若，監察御史李勉奏彈之，繫於有司。

translations.literal: General Guan Chongsi was in the audience hall, seated with his back to the palace gate, speaking and laughing at ease. Supervising Censor Li Mian memorialized impeaching him and had him bound over to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: General Guan Chongsi sat in the audience hall with his back to the palace gate, chatting and laughing as he pleased. Supervising Censor Li Mian impeached him and had him turned over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 上特原之，歎曰：「吾有李勉，朝廷始尊！」

translations.literal: The emperor specially pardoned him and sighed, saying, "With Li Mian, the court is at last respected!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally pardoned Guan Chongsi and exclaimed, "With Li Mian, the court at last commands respect!"

sentences.zh: 勉，元懿之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Mian was the great-grandson of Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian was the great-grandson of Li Yuanyi.

sentences.zh: 旬日間，歸附者漸眾。

translations.literal: Within ten days, those who came over to submit gradually grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days, ever more people came over to submit.

sentences.zh: 張良娣性巧慧，能得上意，從上來朔方。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang Liangdi was clever and quick-witted by nature and could grasp the emperor's intent. She accompanied the emperor coming to Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang Liangdi was clever and quick-witted and knew how to please the emperor. She accompanied him north to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 時從兵單寡，良娣每寢，常居上前。

translations.literal: At that time the accompanying troops were few and sparse; whenever Liangdi slept, she regularly lay ahead of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The escort was thin at the time, and whenever Liangdi slept she would lie in front of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「禦寇非婦人所能。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Repelling bandits is not something women can do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Warding off enemies is no task for a woman."

sentences.zh: 良娣曰：「蒼猝之際，妾以身當之，殿下可從後逸去。」

translations.literal: Liangdi said, "In a moment of sudden crisis, your servant will take the blow herself; Your Highness may slip away from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdi replied, "In a sudden attack I will take the blow myself, and Your Highness can escape from behind."

sentences.zh: 至靈武，產子；

translations.literal: When they reached Lingwu, she gave birth;
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Lingwu she gave birth;

sentences.zh: 三日起，縫戰士衣。

translations.literal: On the third day she rose and sewed soldiers' garments.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day she got up and sewed clothing for the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 上止之，對曰：「此非妾自養之時。」

translations.literal: The emperor tried to stop her; she answered, "This is not the time for your servant to nourish herself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried to stop her. She answered, "This is no time for me to rest and recover."

sentences.zh: 上以是益憐之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore cherished her all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore doted on her all the more.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上皇制：「以太子亨充天下兵馬元帥，領朔方、河東、河北、平盧節度都使，南取長安、洛陽。

translations.literal: On dingmao day, the Retired Emperor issued an edict: "Appoint Crown Prince Heng Commander-in-Chief of All Armies and Horses in the Empire, directing the superintendents of the Shuofang, Hedong, Hebei, and Pinglu military commissions, to march south and recover Chang'an and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day the Retired Emperor issued an edict: "Crown Prince Heng is appointed Commander-in-Chief of all armies and horses in the empire, overseeing the Shuofang, Hedong, Hebei, and Pinglu military superintendents, to march south and retake Chang'an and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以御史中丞裴冕兼左庶子，隴西郡司馬劉秩試守右庶子；

translations.literal: Appoint Supervising Censor Pei Mian concurrently Left Subordinate Heir; Longxi Administrator's Assistant Liu Zhi acting Right Subordinate Heir;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Pei Mian is appointed concurrent Left Subordinate Heir; Longxi Administrator's Assistant Liu Zhi is appointed acting Right Subordinate Heir;

sentences.zh: 永王璘充山南東道、嶺南、黔中、江南西道節度都使，以少府監竇紹為之傅，長沙太守李峴為都副大使；

translations.literal: Prince Yong Li Lin shall serve as superintendent of the Shannan East Circuit, Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jiangnan West Circuit military commissions; appoint Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Household Dou Shao his tutor, and Changsha Administrator Li Xian Grand Deputy Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong Li Lin is appointed superintendent of the Shannan East, Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jiangnan West military commissions; Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Household Dou Shao is appointed his tutor, and Changsha Administrator Li Xian Grand Deputy Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 盛王琦充廣陵大都督，領江南東路及淮南、河南等路節度都使，以前江陵都督府長史劉匯為之傅，廣陵郡長史李成式為都副大使；

translations.literal: Prince Sheng Li Qi shall serve as Grand Governor of Guangling, directing the Jiangnan East Circuit and the Huainan, Henan, and other circuit military superintendents; appoint former Chief Administrator of Jiangling Supervisory Office Liu Hui his tutor, and Guangling Chief Administrator Li Chengshi Grand Deputy Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sheng Li Qi is appointed Grand Governor of Guangling, overseeing the Jiangnan East, Huainan, Henan, and other circuit superintendents; former Chief Administrator of the Jiangling Supervisory Office Liu Hui is appointed his tutor, and Guangling Chief Administrator Li Chengshi Grand Deputy Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 豐王珙充武威都督，仍領河西、隴右、安西、北庭等路節度都使，以隴西太守濟陰鄧景山為之傅，充都副大使。

translations.literal: Prince Feng Li Gong shall serve as Governor of Wuwei, continuing to direct the Hexi, Longyou, Anxi, Beiting, and other circuit military superintendents; appoint Longxi Administrator and former Jiyin official Deng Jingshan his tutor and Grand Deputy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Feng Li Gong is appointed Governor of Wuwei, continuing to oversee the Hexi, Longyou, Anxi, Beiting, and other circuit superintendents; Longxi Administrator and former Jiyin official Deng Jingshan is appointed his tutor and Grand Deputy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 應須士馬、甲仗、糧賜等，並於當路自供。

translations.literal: All needed troops, horses, armor, weapons, grain rations, and gifts shall each be supplied by the circuits concerned.
translations.idiomatic: All required troops, horses, armor, provisions, and supplies are to be furnished locally by each circuit.

sentences.zh: 其諸路本節度使虢王巨等並依前充使。

translations.literal: The original military commissioners of the various circuits, Prince of Guo Ju and others, shall continue in their posts as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The existing circuit commissioners, including Prince of Guo Ju, shall remain in their posts.

sentences.zh: 其署置官屬及本路郡縣官，並任自簡擇，署訖聞奏。」

translations.literal: As for appointing subordinate officials and the officials of commanderies and counties within each circuit, each may freely select them; once appointments are made, report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Each superintendent may freely appoint his own staff and the commandery and county officials on his route, reporting the appointments afterward to the throne."

sentences.zh: 時琦、珙皆不出閣，惟璘赴鎮。

translations.literal: At that time Qi and Gong had still not left the palace residence; only Li Lin went to his post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qi and Gong had not yet left the palace; only Li Lin went to take up his command.

sentences.zh: 置山南東道節度，領襄陽等九郡。

translations.literal: The Shannan East Circuit military commission was established, governing nine commanderies including Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: A Shannan East Circuit military commission was created, governing nine commanderies including Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 升五府經略使為嶺南節度，領南海等二十二郡。

translations.literal: The Five Prefectures Frontier Commissioner was promoted to Lingnan Military Commission, governing twenty-two commanderies including Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Prefectures Frontier Commissioner was elevated to Lingnan Military Commissioner, governing twenty-two commanderies including Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 升五溪經略使為黔中節度，領黔中等諸郡。

translations.literal: The Five Streams Frontier Commissioner was promoted to Qianzhong Military Commission, governing the various commanderies of Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Streams Frontier Commissioner was elevated to Qianzhong Military Commissioner, governing the commanderies of Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 分江南為東、西二道，東道領餘杭，西道領豫章等諸郡。

translations.literal: Jiangnan was divided into Eastern and Western circuits; the Eastern Circuit governed Yuhang, and the Western Circuit governed the various commanderies including Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan was split into eastern and western circuits: the eastern circuit took Yuhang, and the western circuit took Yuzhang and neighboring commanderies.

sentences.zh: 先是四方聞潼關失守，莫知上所之，及是制下，始知乘輿所在。

translations.literal: Earlier, throughout the realm when news came that Tong Pass had fallen, no one knew where the emperor had gone; when this edict was issued, they first learned where the imperial carriage was.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong Pass fell, the empire had not known where the emperor had gone; only when this edict appeared did people learn where the imperial carriage was.

sentences.zh: 匯，秩之弟也。

translations.literal: Hui was the younger brother of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui was Liu Zhi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 安祿山使孫孝哲殺霍國長公主及王妃、附馬等於崇仁坊，刳其心，以祭安慶宗。

translations.literal: An Lushan had Sun Xiaozhe kill the Princess of Huoguo, princesses consort, imperial sons-in-law, and others in Chongren Ward, cut out their hearts, and offer them in sacrifice to An Qingzong.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan had Sun Xiaozhe kill the Princess of Huoguo, consorts, imperial sons-in-law, and others in Chongren Ward, cut out their hearts, and sacrifice them to An Qingzong.

sentences.zh: 凡楊國忠、高力士之黨及祿山素所惡者皆殺之，凡八十三人，或以鐵棓揭其腦蓋，流血滿街。

translations.literal: All who were partisans of Yang Guozhong and Gao Lishi, and all whom Lushan had long detested, were killed—eighty-three persons in all. Some had their skulls smashed open with iron clubs; blood filled the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone tied to Yang Guozhong and Gao Lishi, and everyone Lushan had long hated, was killed—eighty-three people in all. Some had their skulls smashed open with iron clubs until blood ran in the streets.

sentences.zh: 己巳，又殺皇孫及郡、縣主二十餘人。

translations.literal: On jisi day, he again killed more than twenty imperial grandsons and commandery and county princesses.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day he killed more than twenty imperial grandsons and commandery and county princesses.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上皇至巴西；

translations.literal: On gengwu day, the Retired Emperor reached Baxi;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the Retired Emperor reached Baxi;

sentences.zh: 太守崔渙迎謁。

translations.literal: Administrator Cui Huan came out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Cui Huan came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 上皇與語，悅之，房琯復薦之，即日，拜門下侍郎、同平章事，以韋見素為左相。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor spoke with him and was pleased. Fang Guan again recommended him. That same day he was appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Fellow Grand Councillor; Wei Jiansu was made Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor spoke with Cui Huan and was pleased. Fang Guan recommended him again, and that same day Cui Huan was appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Fellow Grand Councillor, with Wei Jiansu as Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 渙，玄□之孫也。

translations.literal: Huan was a grandson of Cui [Xuanwei].
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huan was a grandson of Cui [Xuanwei].

sentences.zh: 初，京兆李泌，幼以才敏著聞，玄宗使與忠王游。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Mi of Jingzhao, famed from youth for talent and quickness, was made to associate with Prince Zhong by Emperor Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi of Jingzhao had been known from youth for quick wit; Emperor Xuanzong had him keep company with Prince Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠王為太子，泌已長，上書言事。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhong became Crown Prince, Mi had already grown up and submitted memorials on public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhong became Crown Prince, Mi was already grown and began submitting memorials on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 玄宗欲官之，不可；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong wished to give him office, but he would not accept;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong wanted to give him office, but Mi refused;

sentences.zh: 使與太子為布衣交，太子常謂之先生。

translations.literal: He had him become a commoner's friend of the Crown Prince; the Crown Prince regularly called him "Master."
translations.idiomatic: Instead the emperor let him become the Crown Prince's friend as a private citizen; the Crown Prince always called him "Master."

sentences.zh: 楊國忠惡之，奏徒蘄春，後得歸隱，居穎陽。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong hated him and memorialized to exile him to Qichun; later he was able to return to seclusion and lived in Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong hated him and had him exiled to Qichun; later Mi was able to retire and lived in seclusion at Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 上自馬嵬北行，遣使召之，謁見於靈武，上大喜，出則聯轡，寢則對榻，如為太子時，事無大小皆咨之，言無不從，至於進退將相亦與之議。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched north from Mawei, he dispatched an envoy to summon him. When Mi had an audience at Lingwu, the emperor was greatly pleased. When they went out they rode side by side; when they slept they shared a couch, just as in the days when he was Crown Prince. On matters great and small he consulted Mi; none of Mi's words went unheeded. Even the appointment and dismissal of generals and chief ministers was discussed with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong marched north from Mawei he sent for Li Mi. Mi had an audience at Lingwu, and the emperor was overjoyed. Out of doors they rode side by side; at night they shared a couch, just as in the Crown Prince's days. The emperor consulted Mi on everything, great or small, and never refused his counsel—even the appointment and dismissal of generals and chief ministers was decided with him.

sentences.zh: 上欲以泌為右相，泌固辭曰：「陛下待以賓友，則貴於宰相矣，何必屈其志！」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Mi Right Chancellor; Mi firmly declined, saying, "If Your Majesty treats me as a guest and friend, that is more honored than being a chief minister—why need you bend my will!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to make Li Mi Right Chancellor. Mi firmly declined: "If Your Majesty treats me as a guest and friend, that is more honor than being a chief minister—why bend my will?"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 同羅、突厥從安祿山反者屯長安苑中，甲戌，其酋長阿史那從禮帥五千騎，竊廄馬二千匹逃歸朔方，謀邀結諸胡，盜據邊地。

translations.literal: The Tongluo and Turks who had followed An Lushan in rebellion were encamped in the parks of Chang'an. On jiaxu day their chieftain Ashina Congli led five thousand horsemen, stole two thousand horses from the stable, and fled back toward Shuofang, plotting to summon and rally the various Hu peoples and seize the borderlands by force.
translations.idiomatic: Tongluo and Turk followers of An Lushan were encamped in the Chang'an imperial parks. On jiaxu day their chieftain Ashina Congli led five thousand horsemen, stole two thousand stable horses, and fled toward Shuofang, planning to rally the frontier tribes and seize the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 上遣使宣慰之，降者甚眾。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to proclaim comfort to them; very many surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to reassure them, and large numbers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 賊遣兵寇扶風，薛景仙擊卻之。

translations.literal: The rebels dispatched troops to raid Fufeng; Xue Jingxian struck and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel troops raided Fufeng; Xue Jingxian beat them back.

sentences.zh: 安祿山遣其將高嵩以敕書、繒彩誘河、隴將士，大震關使郭英乂擒斬之。

translations.literal: An Lushan sent his general Gao Song with an imperial edict and silks to entice the Hedong and Longyou troops; Dazhen Pass Commissioner Guo Yingyi captured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan sent his general Gao Song with an edict and silks to win over the Hedong and Longyou garrisons; Dazhen Pass Commissioner Guo Yingyi captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 同羅、突厥之逃歸也，長安大擾，官吏竄匿，獄囚自出。

translations.literal: When the Tongluo and Turks fled back, Chang'an was greatly disturbed; officials hid themselves, and prisoners broke out of jail on their own.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tongluo and Turks fled, Chang'an was thrown into turmoil: officials went into hiding and prisoners broke out on their own.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹崔光遠以為賊且遁矣，遣吏卒守孫孝哲宅。

translations.literal: Jingzhao Governor Cui Guangyuan thought the rebels were about to flee; he dispatched clerks and soldiers to guard Sun Xiaozhe's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Governor Cui Guangyuan thought the rebels were about to withdraw and sent clerks and soldiers to occupy Sun Xiaozhe's house.

sentences.zh: 孝哲以狀白祿山，光遠乃與長安令蘇震帥府、縣官十餘人來奔。

translations.literal: Xiaozhe reported the situation to Lushan; Guangyuan then led more than ten officials of the prefecture and county, together with Chang'an Magistrate Su Zhen, to flee and come over.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhe reported this to Lushan, whereupon Guangyuan fled with Chang'an Magistrate Su Zhen and more than ten prefectural and county officials to join the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 己卯，至靈武，上以光遠為御史大夫兼京兆尹，使之渭北招集吏民；

translations.literal: On jimao day they reached Lingwu. The emperor made Guangyuan Censor-in-Chief concurrently Jingzhao Governor and sent him north of the Wei to gather officials and people;
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day they reached Lingwu. The emperor made Guangyuan Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Jingzhao Governor, sending him north of the Wei to rally officials and people;

sentences.zh: 以震為中丞。

translations.literal: Zhen was made Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhen was made Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 震，瑰之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhen was the grandson of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhen was the grandson of Su Gui.

sentences.zh: 祿山以田乾真為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Lushan appointed Tian Qianzhen Jingzhao Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan appointed Tian Qianzhen Jingzhao Governor.

sentences.zh: 侍御史呂諲、右拾遺楊綰、奉天令安平崔器相繼詣靈武；

translations.literal: Attending Censor Lü Yin, Right Reminder Yang Wan, and Fengtian Magistrate Anping Cui Qi arrived at Lingwu one after another;
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Lü Yin, Right Reminder Yang Wan, and Fengtian Magistrate Cui Qi of Anping arrived at Lingwu in succession;

sentences.zh: 以諲、器為御史中丞，綰為起居舍人、知制誥。

translations.literal: Yin and Qi were made Vice Censors-in-Chief; Wan was made Drafting Secretary for Imperial Diaries and Controller of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yin and Cui Qi were made Vice Censors-in-Chief; Yang Wan was made Drafting Secretary for Imperial Diaries and Controller of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 上命河西節度副使李嗣業將兵五千赴行在，嗣業與節度使梁宰謀，且緩師以觀變。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Hexi Military Deputy Commissioner Li Siye to lead five thousand troops to the imperial encampment. Siye and Military Commissioner Liang Zai plotted to slow the march and observe how events developed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hexi Deputy Commissioner Li Siye to bring five thousand troops to the imperial camp. Siye and Military Commissioner Liang Zai plotted to delay the march and watch how events unfolded.

sentences.zh: 綏德府折衝段秀實讓嗣業曰：「豈有君父告急而臣子晏然不赴者乎！

translations.literal: Suide Prefecture assault-commander Duan Xiushi reproached Siye, saying, "How can there be a subject who sits at ease and does not go when lord and father are in urgent distress!
translations.idiomatic: Suide Prefecture assault-commander Duan Xiushi rebuked Siye: "How can a subject sit idle when his lord and father are in peril?

sentences.zh: 特進常自謂大丈夫，今日視之，乃兒女子耳！」

translations.literal: You who hold the title Honored One regularly call yourself a great man—in today's view is nothing but a mere woman!
translations.idiomatic: You, an Honored One who always call yourself a great man—today you look like nothing but a weakling!"

sentences.zh: 嗣業大慚，即白宰如數發兵，以秀實自副，將之詣行在。

translations.literal: Siye was greatly ashamed and immediately reported to Zai to dispatch troops according to the original number, making Xiushi his deputy and leading them to the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply ashamed, Siye at once told Liang Zai to send the full force as ordered, made Xiushi his deputy, and marched to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 上又徵兵於安西；

translations.literal: The emperor also requisitioned troops from Anxi;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also called up troops from Anxi;

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬李棲筠發精兵七千人，勵以忠義而遣之。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator's Assistant Li Qiyun mobilized seven thousand elite troops, urged them with appeals to loyalty and righteousness, and dispatched them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator's Assistant Li Qiyun raised seven thousand elite troops, exhorted them with appeals to loyalty and duty, and sent them off.

sentences.zh: 敕改扶風為鳳翔郡。

translations.literal: An edict changed Fufeng to Fengxiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Fufeng as Fengxiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，上皇至成都，從官及六軍至者千三百人而已。

translations.literal: On gengchen day the Retired Emperor reached Chengdu; officials who followed and troops of the Six Armies who arrived numbered only thirteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day the Retired Emperor reached Chengdu; only thirteen hundred followers and Six Armies troops had made it there.

sentences.zh: 令狐潮圍張巡於雍丘，相守四十餘日，朝廷聲問不通。

translations.literal: Linghu Chao besieged Zhang Xun at Yongqiu; they faced each other for more than forty days, and no word from the court got through.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao besieged Zhang Xun at Yongqiu. The siege lasted more than forty days with no word from the court.

sentences.zh: 潮聞玄宗已幸蜀，復以書招巡。

translations.literal: Chao heard that Emperor Xuanzong had already proceeded to Shu and again sent a letter to entice Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Chao heard that Emperor Xuanzong had already gone to Shu and again wrote to win Zhang Xun over.

sentences.zh: 有大將六人，官皆開府、特進，白巡以兵勢不敵，且上存亡不可知，不如降賊。

translations.literal: There were six senior generals, all holding the ranks of Kaifu and Tejin, who told Xun that their military strength could not match the enemy, and that whether the emperor lived or died was unknown—it would be better to surrender to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Six senior generals, all holding Kaifu and Tejin rank, told Xun that they were outmatched and that the emperor's fate was unknown—it would be better to surrender.

sentences.zh: 巡陽許諾。

translations.literal: Xun falsely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 明日，堂上設天子畫像，帥將士朝之，人人皆泣。

translations.literal: The next day he set up the emperor's portrait in the hall, led the officers and soldiers to pay court to it, and everyone wept.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he set the emperor's portrait in the hall, led his officers and men to bow before it, and everyone wept.

sentences.zh: 巡引六將於前，責以大義，斬之。

translations.literal: Xun brought the six generals forward, rebuked them on grounds of righteousness, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun brought the six generals forward, rebuked them for betraying their duty, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 士心益勸。

translations.literal: The soldiers' hearts were all the more encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: The troops' morale rose all the higher.

sentences.zh: 中城矢盡，巡縛蒿為人千餘，被以黑衣，夜縋城下，潮兵爭射之，久乃知其蒿人；

translations.literal: When arrows in the inner city were exhausted, Xun bound artemisia into more than a thousand human figures, clothed them in black garments, and lowered them down the wall by night. Chao's troops vied to shoot them; only after a long while did they realize they were artemisia figures;
translations.idiomatic: When the inner city's arrows ran out, Zhang Xun tied more than a thousand scarecrows from artemisia stalks, dressed them in black, and lowered them down the wall by night. Chao's men shot at them furiously; only after a long while did they realize they were dummy figures;

sentences.zh: 得矢數十萬。

translations.literal: They obtained several hundred thousand arrows.
translations.idiomatic: and recovered several hundred thousand arrows.

sentences.zh: 其後復夜縋人，賊笑不設備，乃以死士五百斫潮營；

translations.literal: Afterward they again lowered men down by night; the rebels laughed and made no preparations. Then with five hundred death-defying soldiers they stormed Chao's camp;
translations.idiomatic: Later they lowered men down again by night; the rebels laughed and let their guard down. Then five hundred picked men raided Chao's camp;

sentences.zh: 潮軍大亂，焚壘而遁，追奔十餘里。

translations.literal: Chao's army fell into great disorder, burned their fortifications and fled; they pursued the routed enemy for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's army broke in panic, burned its camp, and fled; the Tang force pursued them more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 潮慚，益兵圍之。

translations.literal: Chao was ashamed and increased his troops to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Chao brought up more troops to tighten the siege.

sentences.zh: 巡使郎將雷萬春於城上與潮相聞，語未絕，賊弩射之，面中六矢而不動。

translations.literal: Xun had Commandant Lei Wanchun exchange shouts with Chao atop the wall. Before the words were finished, rebel crossbows shot him; six arrows struck his face, yet he did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun had Commandant Lei Wanchun shout back and forth with Chao from the wall. Before he finished speaking, rebel crossbowmen shot him; six bolts struck his face, yet he did not stir.

sentences.zh: 潮疑其木人，使諜問之，乃大驚，遙謂巡曰：「向見雷將軍，方知足下軍令矣，然其如天道何！」

translations.literal: Chao suspected he was a wooden man and sent a spy to ask; he was greatly startled and called out from afar to Xun: "Just now I saw General Lei and knew that Your Honor's military discipline is firm—but what can be done about the Mandate of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Chao thought he was a wooden dummy and sent a spy to check; then, greatly startled, he shouted to Zhang Xun from afar: "Just now I saw General Lei and knew your discipline is iron—but what can anyone do against Heaven's mandate?"

sentences.zh: 巡謂之曰：「君未識人倫，焉知天道！」

translations.literal: Xun said to him: "You do not yet understand human relations—how can you know the Mandate of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun replied: "You do not even understand human duty—how can you speak of Heaven's mandate?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，出戰，擒賊將十四人，斬道百餘級。

translations.literal: Before long they went out to battle, captured fourteen rebel generals, and cut down more than a hundred heads along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they sallied out, captured fourteen rebel officers, and killed more than a hundred men on the road.

sentences.zh: 賊乃夜遁，收兵入陳留，不敢復出。

translations.literal: The rebels then fled by night, gathered their troops into Chenliu, and dared not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew by night, pulled their forces back into Chenliu, and did not dare come out again.

sentences.zh: 頃之，賊步騎七千餘眾屯白沙渦，巡夜襲擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, more than seven thousand rebel infantry and cavalry encamped at Baisha Bend; Xun attacked by night and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward more than seven thousand rebel foot and horse encamped at Baisha Bend; Zhang Xun attacked by night and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 還，至桃陵，遇賊救兵四百餘人，悉擒之。

translations.literal: Returning, when they reached Taoling they encountered more than four hundred rebel relief troops and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, at Taoling they met more than four hundred rebel reinforcements and took them all.

sentences.zh: 分別其眾，媯、檀及胡兵，悉斬之；

translations.literal: Separating the captives, they beheaded all the Gui, Tan, and Hu troops;
translations.idiomatic: Sorting the prisoners, they executed all the Gui, Tan, and Hu soldiers;

sentences.zh: 滎陽、陳留脅從兵，皆散令歸業。

translations.literal: The conscript soldiers of Xingyang and Chenliu were all dispersed and ordered to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: the pressed men of Xingyang and Chenliu were disbanded and sent home to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 旬日間，民去賊來歸者萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Within ten days, more than ten thousand households of people who had left the rebels came back.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days more than ten thousand households that had submitted to the rebels came back over to Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 河北諸郡猶為唐守，常山太守王輔欲降賊，諸將怒，因擊球，縱馬踐殺之。

translations.literal: The various commanderies of Hebei still held for Tang. Changshan Administrator Wang Fu wished to surrender to the rebels; the generals were enraged and therefore struck him, trampled him with horses, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei commanderies still held for Tang. Changshan Administrator Wang Fu wanted to surrender to the rebels; the generals were furious, struck him, trampled him under their horses, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時信都太守烏承恩麾下有朔方兵三千人，諸將遣使者宗仙運帥父老詣信都，迎承恩鎮常山。

translations.literal: At that time Xindu Administrator Wu Cheng'en had three thousand Shuofang troops under his command; the generals sent the envoy Zong Xianyun to lead the elders to Xindu to welcome Cheng'en to take charge at Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xindu Administrator Wu Cheng'en had three thousand Shuofang troops under his command. The generals sent the envoy Zong Xianyun, leading local elders, to Xindu to welcome Cheng'en and install him as commander at Changshan.

sentences.zh: 承恩辭以無詔命，仙運說承恩曰：「常山地控燕、薊，路通河、洛，有井陘之險，足以扼其咽喉。

translations.literal: Cheng'en declined on the grounds that there was no imperial edict; Xianyun persuaded Cheng'en, saying, "Changshan commands Yan and Ji, its roads connect to the He and Luo regions, and it holds the peril of Jingxing Pass—enough to throttle the enemy's throat.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en declined, citing the lack of an imperial order. Xianyun urged him: "Changshan overlooks Yan and Ji, its roads link the He and Luo valleys, and Jingxing Pass gives it a choke point strong enough to grip the enemy by the throat.

sentences.zh: 頃屬車駕南遷，李大夫收軍退守晉陽，王太守權統後軍，欲舉城降賊，眾心不從，身首異處。

translations.literal: Recently, when the imperial carriage moved south, Grandee Li gathered the army and withdrew to defend Jinyang; Administrator Wang temporarily commanded the rear guard, wished to surrender the city to the rebels, the hearts of the masses would not follow, and he ended with body and head in different places.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, when the court moved south, Grandee Li withdrew his forces to hold Jinyang. Administrator Wang, who had temporarily commanded the rear guard, tried to surrender the city to the rebels; the men refused to follow him, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 大將軍兵精氣肅，遠近莫敵，若以家國為念，移據常山，與大夫首尾相應，則洪勳盛烈，孰與為比！

translations.literal: The Grand General's troops are elite and their spirit stern; none near or far can match them. If you keep family and state in mind, shift your base to Changshan, and coordinate with the Grandee from front to rear, then what great merit and blazing achievement could compare!
translations.idiomatic: Your troops are elite and disciplined, unmatched anywhere near or far. If you act for family and state, move to Changshan and coordinate with the Grandee in a pincer, your achievement will be beyond compare!

sentences.zh: 若疑而不行，又不設備，常山既陷，信都豈能獨全！」

translations.literal: If you hesitate and do not go, and also make no preparations—once Changshan falls, how can Xindu alone remain intact!"
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate, fail to move, and leave yourself unprepared, once Changshan falls Xindu cannot stand alone!"

sentences.zh: 承恩不從。

translations.literal: Cheng'en did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en would not agree.

sentences.zh: 仙運又曰：「將軍不納鄙夫之言，必懼兵少故也。

translations.literal: Xianyun again said, "The General does not accept this humble man's words—surely it is because he fears having too few troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyun added: "If you reject my counsel, General, it must be because you fear your force is too small.

sentences.zh: 今人不聊生，鹹思報國，競相結聚，屯據鄉村，若懸賞招之，不旬日十萬可致；

translations.literal: Now the people cannot make a living; all long to repay the state, competing to gather and encamp in villages and hamlets—if rewards are posted to recruit them, within ten days one hundred thousand can be obtained;
translations.idiomatic: The people are destitute and eager to serve the dynasty; they are rallying in villages throughout the countryside. Offer bounties to recruit them, and within ten days you can raise a hundred thousand men;

sentences.zh: 與朔方甲士三千餘人相參用之，足成王事。

translations.literal: used together with the more than three thousand armored Shuofang soldiers, this is enough to accomplish the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: combined with your three thousand Shuofang veterans, that would be enough to restore the throne.

sentences.zh: 若捨要害以授人，居四通而自安，譬如倒持劍戟，取敗之道也。」

translations.literal: If you abandon the strategic point and hand it to others, dwelling at a crossroads while seeking your own ease, it is like holding sword and halberd by the blade—the way to invite defeat."
translations.idiomatic: To abandon a key stronghold to others while you settle at a crossroads and seek safety is like holding a sword by the blade—the sure path to defeat."

sentences.zh: 承恩竟疑不決。

translations.literal: In the end Cheng'en remained doubtful and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Cheng'en wavered and never made up his mind.

sentences.zh: 承恩，承玼族兄也。

translations.literal: Cheng'en was a clan elder brother of Cheng Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en was an elder cousin of Cheng Ci.

sentences.zh: 是月，史思明、蔡希德將兵萬人南攻九門。

translations.literal: That month, Shi Siming and Cai Xide led ten thousand troops south to attack Jiumen.
translations.idiomatic: That month Shi Siming and Cai Xide marched south with ten thousand men to attack Jiumen.

sentences.zh: 旬日，九門偽降，伏甲於城上。

translations.literal: After ten days Jiumen feigned surrender and hid armored troops atop the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Jiumen pretended to surrender and concealed armored men on the walls.

sentences.zh: 思明登城，伏兵攻之；

translations.literal: Siming ascended the wall, and the ambush troops attacked him;
translations.idiomatic: When Siming climbed the wall, the hidden troops struck;

sentences.zh: 思明墜城，鹿角傷其左脅，夜，奔博陵。

translations.literal: Siming fell from the wall; chevaux-de-frise wounded his left flank; by night he fled to Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Siming fell from the ramparts; field obstacles gashed his left side. That night he fled to Boling.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿以蠟丸達表於靈武。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing sent a memorial to Lingwu enclosed in a wax pellet.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing smuggled a memorial to Lingwu inside a wax pellet.

sentences.zh: 以真卿為工部尚書兼御史大夫，依前河北招討、採訪、處置使，並致赦書，亦以蠟丸達之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing was appointed Minister of Works and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, continuing as before as Hebei Recruit-and-Pacify, Investigation, and Disposition Commissioner; an amnesty edict was also sent, likewise delivered by wax pellet.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Zhenqing Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief, confirmed him in his former posts as Hebei Recruit-and-Pacify, Investigation, and Disposition Commissioner, and sent an amnesty edict by the same wax-pellet route.

sentences.zh: 真卿頒下河北諸郡，又遣人頒於河南、江、淮。

translations.literal: Zhenqing promulgated it throughout the commanderies of Hebei, and also sent men to promulgate it in Henan, the Yangzi region, and the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing distributed the edicts across Hebei and dispatched couriers to circulate them in Henan, the Yangzi valley, and the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 由是諸道始知上即位於靈武，徇國之心益堅矣。

translations.literal: From this the various circuits first learned that the emperor had ascended the throne at Lingwu, and hearts devoted to the state grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the provinces learn that the emperor had taken the throne at Lingwu, and loyalty to the dynasty strengthened everywhere.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀等將兵五萬自河北至靈武，靈武軍威始盛，人有興復之望矣。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi and others led fifty thousand troops from Hebei to Lingwu; the military prestige of Lingwu began to flourish, and people had hope of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi and others brought fifty thousand troops from Hebei to Lingwu. Lingwu's military strength swelled at last, and people began to hope for restoration.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬午朔，以子儀為武部尚書、靈武長史，以李光弼為戶部尚書、北都留守，並同平章事，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of the cycle renwu, Ziyi was made Minister of War and Chief Administrator of Lingwu; Li Guangbi was made Minister of Revenue and Northern Capital Protector; both were made Fellows of the Secretariat with the same rank as Counselors of State; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the new moon of the day renwu, Ziyi was appointed Minister of War and chief administrator of Lingwu; Li Guangbi was appointed Minister of Revenue and protector of the Northern Capital; both were made chief ministers with the rank of Counselor of State, and their other duties were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 光弼以景城、河間兵五千赴太原。

translations.literal: Guangbi took five thousand troops from Jingcheng and Hejian and went to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi marched five thousand men from Jingcheng and Hejian to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，河東節度使王承業軍政不修，朝廷遣待御史崔眾交其兵，尋遣中使誅之；

translations.literal: Earlier, Hedong Military Commissioner Wang Chengye had not kept military and civil affairs in order; the court sent Attending Censor Cui Zhong to take over his troops, and soon sent a palace envoy to execute him;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hedong Military Commissioner Wang Chengye had neglected military and civil administration. The court sent Attending Censor Cui Zhong to take command of his army, then dispatched a palace envoy to execute him;

sentences.zh: 眾侮易承業，光弼素不平。

translations.literal: Zhong treated Chengye with contempt and disrespect; Guangbi had long been displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong openly humiliated Chengye, which Guangbi had resented for some time.

sentences.zh: 至是，敕交兵於光弼，眾見光弼，不為禮，又不時交兵，光弼怒，收斬之，軍中股慄。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered the transfer of troops to Guangbi; when Zhong met Guangbi he showed no courtesy, and also did not hand over the troops promptly; Guangbi, enraged, had him seized and beheaded, and the army trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered the troops transferred to Guangbi. When Zhong appeared before him, he showed no respect and delayed handing over the army. Guangbi, furious, had him arrested and executed, and the whole force quaked.

sentences.zh: 回紇可汗、吐蕃贊普相繼遣使請助國討賊，宴賜而遣之。

translations.literal: The Uyghur khan and the Tibetan tsenpo successively sent envoys requesting to aid the state in suppressing the rebels; they were feasted, rewarded, and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur khan and the Tibetan tsenpo sent envoys in succession offering to help the dynasty crush the rebels. The court entertained them, bestowed gifts, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 癸未，上皇下制，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, the Retired Emperor issued an edict amnestying all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei the Retired Emperor issued an edict granting a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 北海太守賀蘭進明遣錄事參軍第五琦入蜀奏事，琦言於上皇，以為：「今方用兵，財賦為急，財賦所產，江、淮居多，乞假臣一職，可使軍無乏用。」

translations.literal: Beihai Administrator Helan Jinming sent Recording Officer Diwu Qi into Shu to report on affairs; Qi spoke to the Retired Emperor, saying, "We are now at war, and revenue is urgent; revenue is produced mostly in the Jiang and Huai regions—I beg to be granted one office so that the army may never lack supplies."
translations.idiomatic: Beihai Administrator Helan Jinming sent Recording Officer Diwu Qi to Shu to report to the Retired Emperor. Qi argued: "With war underway, finance is the urgent need, and most revenue comes from the Jiang and Huai regions. Grant me an office, and I can keep the armies supplied."

sentences.zh: 上皇悅，即以琦為監察御史、江淮租庸使。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor was pleased and immediately appointed Qi Attending Censor and Jiang-Huai Tax-and-Corvée Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor was pleased and at once appointed Qi Attending Censor and commissioner of Jiang-Huai taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 史思明再攻九門，辛卯，克之，所殺數千人；

translations.literal: Shi Siming again attacked Jiumen; on the day xinmao he captured it and killed several thousand people;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming attacked Jiumen again. On the day xinmao he took the city and slaughtered several thousand people;

sentences.zh: 引兵東圍蒿城。

translations.literal: he led his troops east to besiege Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: then marched east to besiege Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 李庭望將蕃、漢二萬餘人東襲寧陵、襄邑，夜，去雍丘城三十里置營。

translations.literal: Li Tingwang led more than twenty thousand Tibetan and Han troops east to strike Ningling and Xiangyi; by night he encamped thirty li from Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingwang led more than twenty thousand Tibetan and Han troops east against Ningling and Xiangyi. By night he made camp thirty li from Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 張巡帥短兵三千掩擊，大破之，殺獲太半。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun led three thousand short weapons in a surprise attack, inflicted a great defeat, and killed or captured more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun struck with three thousand hand-picked troops in a night raid, routing them and killing or capturing more than half their force.

sentences.zh: 庭望收軍夜遁。

translations.literal: Tingwang gathered his army and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Tingwang regrouped what he could and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，靈武使者至蜀，上皇喜曰：「吾兒應天順人，吾復何憂！」

translations.literal: On the day guisi, an envoy from Lingwu reached Shu; the Retired Emperor said with joy, "My son has answered Heaven and followed the people—what have I left to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi an envoy from Lingwu reached Shu. The Retired Emperor rejoiced: "My son has answered Heaven and won the people's assent—what more have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 丁酉，制：「自今改制敕為誥，表疏稱太上皇。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, an edict stated: "From now on, change the term zhi into gao; memorials and reports shall address the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou he decreed: "Henceforth edicts shall be styled gao, and memorials shall address me as the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 四海軍國事，皆先取皇帝進止，仍奏朕知；

translations.literal: All military and state affairs within the Four Seas shall first follow the emperor's decision, and still be reported to Us for Our knowledge;
translations.idiomatic: All military and state affairs throughout the realm shall first await the emperor's decision, though they are still to be reported to me;

sentences.zh: 俟克復上京，朕不復預事。」

translations.literal: when the Upper Capital is recovered, We shall no longer intervene in affairs."
translations.idiomatic: once the capital is recovered, I shall withdraw from affairs altogether."

sentences.zh: 己亥，上皇臨軒，命韋見素、房琯、崔渙奉傳國寶玉冊詣靈武傳位。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, the Retired Emperor appeared at the imperial hall and ordered Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Huan to carry the imperial seal and jade register to Lingwu to transmit the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jihai the Retired Emperor appeared at court and ordered Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Huan to carry the imperial seal and jade register to Lingwu to abdicate in his son's favor.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，史思明陷蒿城。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Shi Siming captured Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou Shi Siming took Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 初，上皇每酺宴，先設太常雅樂坐部、立部，繼以鼓吹、胡樂、教坊、府縣散樂、雜戲；

translations.literal: Earlier, whenever the Retired Emperor held a feast of universal rejoicing, he first set out the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' refined music in seated and standing sections, followed by wind-and-percussion, foreign music, the Music Bureau, miscellaneous music from prefectures and counties, and variety acts;
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, whenever the Retired Emperor held a grand banquet, he began with the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' refined seated and standing ensembles, then added military bands, foreign music, Music Bureau pieces, local entertainments, and variety acts;

sentences.zh: 又以山車、陸船載樂往來；

translations.literal: he also had mountain carts and land boats carry musicians back and forth;
translations.idiomatic: he had mountain carts and land boats carry musicians to and fro;

sentences.zh: 又出宮人舞《霓裳羽衣》；

translations.literal: he also brought out palace women to dance "Rainbow Skirts and Feathered Robes";
translations.idiomatic: he sent palace women to dance Rainbow Skirts and Feathered Robes;

sentences.zh: 又教舞馬百匹，銜杯上壽；

translations.literal: he also trained one hundred dancing horses to hold cups in their mouths and offer long life;
translations.idiomatic: he trained a hundred dancing horses to hold cups in their teeth and offer toasts;

sentences.zh: 又引犀、象入場，或拜，或舞。

translations.literal: he also led rhinoceroses and elephants into the arena, some bowing, some dancing.
translations.idiomatic: he even brought rhinoceroses and elephants into the arena to bow or dance.

sentences.zh: 安祿山見而悅之，既克長安，命搜捕樂工，運載樂器、舞衣，驅舞馬、犀、象皆詣洛陽。

translations.literal: An Lushan saw this and was pleased; once he had captured Chang'an, he ordered musicians hunted down and captured, instruments and dance robes transported, and dancing horses, rhinoceroses, and elephants driven all to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan saw all this and was delighted. After taking Chang'an he had musicians rounded up, instruments and costumes shipped, and the dancing horses, rhinoceroses, and elephants driven to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：聖人以道德為麗，仁義為樂；

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: The sage takes virtue and the Way as adornment, and benevolence and righteousness as music;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Guang observes: The sage finds adornment in virtue and the Way, and delight in benevolence and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 故雖茅茨土階，惡衣菲食，不恥其陋，惟恐奉養之過以勞民費財。

translations.literal: therefore even with thatched roofs and earthen steps, coarse clothes and meager food, he is not ashamed of their plainness, fearing only that excessive provision may burden the people and waste wealth.
translations.idiomatic: so even with a thatched roof and earthen steps, coarse clothes and plain food, he feels no shame at their austerity, fearing only that lavish display will burden the people and waste the treasury.

sentences.zh: 明皇恃其承平，不思後患，殫耳目之玩，窮聲技之巧，自謂帝王富貴皆不我如，欲使前莫能及，後無以逾，非徒娛己，亦以誇人。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming relied on long peace and did not think of later troubles; he exhausted pleasures for eye and ear and pushed the arts of sound and skill to their limit, believing that no imperial wealth and honor matched his own, wishing that none before could equal him and none after could surpass him—not merely to amuse himself, but also to dazzle others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, secure in long peace, gave no thought to what might follow. He exhausted every spectacle for eye and ear and pushed music and craft to their limits, convinced that no emperor had ever been so rich or grand. He wanted no predecessor to match him and no successor to exceed him—not merely to please himself, but to dazzle the world.

sentences.zh: 豈知大盜在旁，已有窺窬之心，卒致鑾輿播越，生民塗炭。

translations.literal: How could he know that a great robber was at his side, already harboring thoughts of covetous intrusion, until at last the imperial carriage was driven into exile and the living people were scorched and trampled.
translations.idiomatic: He never imagined that a great bandit stood beside him, already eyeing his throne, until the imperial carriage was driven into exile and the people were plunged into misery.

sentences.zh: 乃知人君崇華靡以示人，適足為大盜之招也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that when a ruler exalts splendor and extravagance to display it before others, he merely invites the great robber.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that when a ruler flaunts luxury to impress others, he is only inviting the great bandit.

sentences.zh: 祿山宴其群臣於凝碧池，盛奏眾樂；

translations.literal: Lushan feasted his ministers at Ningbi Pool with a full performance of many kinds of music;
translations.idiomatic: Lushan entertained his ministers at Ningbi Pool with a lavish musical performance;

sentences.zh: 梨園弟子往往歔欷泣下，賊皆露刃睨之。

translations.literal: Pear Garden disciples often sobbed and wept; the rebels all bared their blades and glared at them.
translations.idiomatic: Pear Garden performers often broke down in sobs; the rebels bared their blades and glared at them.

sentences.zh: 樂工雷海清不勝悲憤，擲樂器於地，西向慟哭。

translations.literal: The musician Lei Haiqing, unable to bear grief and rage, threw his instrument to the ground and wailed facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The musician Lei Haiqing, overcome with grief and fury, hurled his instrument to the ground and wailed toward the west.

sentences.zh: 祿山怒，縛於試馬殿前，支解之。

translations.literal: Lushan, enraged, had him bound before the Horse-Trial Hall and dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan, furious, had him bound before the Horse-Trial Hall and torn limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 祿山聞向日百姓乘亂多盜庫物，既得長安，命大索三日，並其私財盡掠之。

translations.literal: Lushan heard that earlier the common people, taking advantage of the chaos, had stolen much from the storehouses; once he held Chang'an, he ordered a great search for three days and plundered all their private wealth as well.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan learned that during the chaos the people had looted the treasuries. After taking Chang'an he ordered a three-day dragnet and seized their private property as well.

sentences.zh: 又令府縣推按，銖兩之物無不窮治，連引搜捕，支蔓無窮，民間騷然，益思唐室。

translations.literal: He also ordered prefectures and counties to investigate and interrogate; not even items worth a mace or a tael escaped exhaustive prosecution; linked denunciations led to endless searches and arrests; the populace was in uproar and longed all the more for the house of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered prefectures and counties to investigate every case down to the last mace and tael. Denunciations spread in chains, searches never ended, the people seethed, and loyalty to Tang only grew.

sentences.zh: 自上離馬嵬北行，民間相傳太子北收兵來取長安，長安民日夜望之，或時相驚曰：「太子大軍至矣！」

translations.literal: From the time the emperor left Mawei and traveled north, rumor among the people held that the Crown Prince was gathering troops in the north to retake Chang'an; the people of Chang'an watched day and night, and sometimes cried out to one another in alarm, "The Crown Prince's great army has arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor left Mawei and marched north, word spread that the Crown Prince was raising troops in the north to retake Chang'an. The people of Chang'an watched day and night, and sometimes panicked one another with shouts: "The Crown Prince's army is here!"

sentences.zh: 則皆走，市裡為空，賊望見北方塵起，輒驚欲走。

translations.literal: then all would flee, the markets and lanes emptied, and when the rebels saw dust rising in the north they would panic and want to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone would run; streets emptied. When the rebels saw dust rising in the north they panicked and prepared to flee.

sentences.zh: 京畿豪傑往往殺賊官吏，遙應官軍；

translations.literal: Heroes of the capital region often killed rebel officials and responded from afar to the government army;
translations.idiomatic: Bold men around the capital often killed rebel officials and rallied to the imperial armies from afar;

sentences.zh: 誅而復起，相繼不絕，賊不能制。

translations.literal: executed and rising again, succeeding one another without end—the rebels could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: they were cut down only to rise again, one after another, and the rebels could not suppress them.

sentences.zh: 其始自京畿、鄜、坊至於岐、隴皆附之，至是西門之外率為敵壘，賊兵力所及者，南不出武關，北不過雲陽，西不過武功。

translations.literal: At first from the capital region, Fu, and Fang as far as Qi and Long all attached themselves; by this time outside the western gate were mostly enemy camps; where rebel military strength reached, south they did not pass Wuguan, north they did not pass Yunyang, west they did not pass Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: At first the capital region, Fu, Fang, and lands as far as Qi and Long all rallied to the cause. Now enemy camps ringed the city west of the western gate. Where rebel power still held, it reached no farther south than Wuguan, no farther north than Yunyang, and no farther west than Wugong.

sentences.zh: 江、淮奏請貢獻之蜀、之靈武者，皆自襄陽取上津路抵扶風，道路無壅，皆薛景仙之功也。

translations.literal: Tribute and petitions from the Jiang and Huai sent to Shu and to Lingwu all took the Shangjin route from Xiangyang to reach Fufeng; the roads were unobstructed—all the achievement of Xue Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute and memorials from the Jiang and Huai bound for Shu and Lingwu all traveled from Xiangyang by the Shangjin road to Fufeng without obstruction—thanks entirely to Xue Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬子，史思明圍趙郡，丙辰，拔之；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day renzi, Shi Siming besieged Zhao Commandery; on the day bingchen he captured it;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day renzi, Shi Siming besieged Zhao Commandery. On the day bingchen he took it;

sentences.zh: 又圍常山，旬日，城陷，殺數千人。

translations.literal: he again besieged Changshan; after ten days the city fell and several thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: then besieged Changshan. Ten days later the city fell and several thousand were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 建寧王倓，性英果，有才略，從上自馬嵬北行，兵眾寡弱，屢逢寇盜。

translations.literal: Prince of Jianning Tan was by nature brave and resolute, with talent and strategy; he followed the emperor north from Mawei; the army was few and weak and repeatedly encountered bandits and robbers.
