translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jianning Tan was bold, resolute, and gifted with strategy. He accompanied the emperor north from Mawei when the force was small and weak and bandits struck again and again.

sentences.zh: 人炎自選驍勇，居上前後，血戰以衛上。

translations.literal: Ren Yan personally selected the brave and fierce, stationed them before and behind the emperor, and fought in bloody battle to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan personally picked the bravest men, placed them before and behind the emperor, and fought through blood to protect him.

sentences.zh: 上或過時求食，倓悲泣不自勝，軍中皆屬目向之。

translations.literal: When the emperor sometimes went too long without food, Tan wept in grief beyond control, and everyone in the army turned their eyes toward him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went hungry for lack of provisions, Tan wept uncontrollably, and the whole army watched him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 上欲以倓為天下兵馬元帥，使統諸將東征，李泌曰：「建寧誠元帥才；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Tan Grand Marshal of All Armies under Heaven and have him command the generals in an eastern campaign; Li Bi said, "Jianning truly has the talent of a marshal;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to make Tan supreme commander of all armies and send him east to lead the generals. Li Bi said, "Jianning truly has the makings of a commander-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 然廣平，兄也。

translations.literal: yet Guangping is his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: but Guangping is his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 若建寧功成，豈可使廣平為吳太伯乎！」

translations.literal: If Jianning achieves success, how could Guangping be made into a Wu Taibo!"
translations.idiomatic: If Jianning wins glory, can you leave Guangping in the role of Wu Taibo?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「廣平，塚嗣也，何必以元帥為重！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Guangping is the heir in the main line—why must the marshal's post weigh so heavily!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Guangping is the heir apparent—why should the command matter so much!"

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「廣平未正位東宮。

translations.literal: Bi said, "Guangping has not yet been formally established in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Guangping has not yet been formally installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 今天下艱難，眾心所屬，在於元帥。

translations.literal: Now the realm is in hardship; the hearts of the masses attach themselves to the marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in crisis, and men's hopes now attach to whoever holds the command.

sentences.zh: 若建寧大功既成，陛下雖欲不以為儲副，同立功者其肯已乎！

translations.literal: If Jianning's great achievement is complete, even if Your Majesty wishes not to make him heir, would those who shared in the achievement be willing to stop!
translations.idiomatic: If Jianning wins a great victory, even if Your Majesty does not wish to name him heir, will the men who fought beside him accept that?

sentences.zh: 太宗、上皇，即其事也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong and the Retired Emperor are exactly that case."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong and the Retired Emperor are the very precedents."

sentences.zh: 上乃以廣平王俶為天下兵馬元帥，諸將皆以屬焉。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon made Prince of Guangping Xu Grand Marshal of All Armies under Heaven, and all the generals were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed Prince of Guangping Xu supreme commander, and all the generals were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 倓聞之，謝泌曰：「此固倓之心也！」

translations.literal: When Tan heard this, he thanked Bi, saying, "This was indeed Tan's own wish!"
translations.idiomatic: When Tan heard the news, he thanked Bi: "That was always my wish!"

sentences.zh: 上與泌出行軍，軍士指之，竊言曰：「衣黃者，聖人也。

translations.literal: The emperor and Bi went out among the army; soldiers pointed at them and whispered, "The one in yellow is the sage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Bi walked among the troops. Soldiers pointed and whispered: "The man in yellow is the sage.

sentences.zh: 衣白者，山人也。」

translations.literal: The one in white is the mountain man."
translations.idiomatic: The man in white is the mountain recluse."

sentences.zh: 上聞之，以告泌，曰：「艱難之際，不敢相屈以官，且衣紫袍以絕群疑。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and told Bi, saying, "In these hard times I did not dare to press you into office, yet wear a purple robe to end the crowd's doubts."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and told Bi: "In these hard times I did not wish to press you into office, but put on a purple robe to quiet the rumors."

sentences.zh: 泌不得已，受之；

translations.literal: Bi, unable to refuse, accepted it;
translations.idiomatic: Bi, unable to refuse, accepted it;

sentences.zh: 服之，入謝。

translations.literal: put it on and entered to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: donned it and came in to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「既服此，豈可無名稱！」

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said, "Since you wear this, how can you go without a title!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled: "Once you wear this, you cannot go without a title!"

sentences.zh: 出懷中敕，以泌為侍謀軍國、元帥府行軍長史。

translations.literal: He took an edict from his bosom and appointed Bi Staff Strategist for State and Army Affairs and Chief Administrator on Campaign of the Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He produced an edict from his robe and appointed Bi staff strategist for state and army affairs and chief administrator on campaign at the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 泌固辭，上曰：「朕非敢相臣，以濟艱難耳。

translations.literal: Bi firmly declined; the emperor said, "We do not dare to treat you as a minister—we do this only to get through hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Bi refused again. The emperor said, "I am not trying to bind you as a minister—I only need your help through the crisis.

sentences.zh: 俟賊平，任行高志。」

translations.literal: When the rebels are pacified, go wherever your lofty will takes you."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels are crushed, you may follow your own high purpose."

sentences.zh: 泌乃受之。

translations.literal: Bi then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Bi accepted at last.

sentences.zh: 置元帥府於禁中，俶入則泌在府，泌入俶亦如之。

translations.literal: The marshal's headquarters was set up within the palace precinct; when Xu entered, Bi was at headquarters, and when Bi entered, Xu was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal's headquarters was established inside the palace. When Xu went in, Bi remained at headquarters; when Bi went in, Xu did the same.

sentences.zh: 泌又言於上曰：「諸將畏憚天威，在陛下前敷陳軍事，或不能盡所懷；

translations.literal: Bi also spoke to the emperor, saying, "The generals fear and revere imperial majesty; before Your Majesty when they set forth military affairs, they may not fully express what is in their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: Bi also told the emperor: "The generals stand in awe of your majesty. Before you they may not speak their minds fully on military matters;

sentences.zh: 萬一小差，為害甚大。

translations.literal: if there is even a small error, the harm will be very great.
translations.idiomatic: even a small mistake could do great harm.

sentences.zh: 乞先令與臣及廣平熟議，臣與廣平從容奏聞，可者行之，不可者已之。」

translations.literal: I beg that they first be ordered to discuss thoroughly with me and Guangping; I and Guangping will calmly report to Your Majesty—what is acceptable shall be carried out, what is not shall be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Let them first discuss matters fully with Guangping and me. We will then report calmly to you: what is sound will be done, what is not will be dropped."

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅務繁，四方奏報，自昏至曉無虛刻，上悉使送府，泌先開視，有急切者及烽火，重封，隔門通進，餘則待明。

translations.literal: At that time military affairs were pressing; reports from all quarters from dusk to dawn left no idle moment; the emperor had them all sent to headquarters; Bi opened and read them first—those that were urgent or beacon-fire reports he resealed and passed through the gate; the rest waited until daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Military business was urgent; dispatches from every quarter arrived from dusk to dawn without pause. The emperor had them all sent to headquarters. Bi opened them first: urgent items and beacon reports he resealed and passed through the gate at once; the rest waited until morning.

sentences.zh: 禁門鑰契，悉委俶與泌掌之。

translations.literal: The keys and tally-slips of the forbidden gates were all entrusted to Xu and Bi to hold.
translations.idiomatic: The keys and tally-slips to the palace gates were entrusted entirely to Xu and Bi.

sentences.zh: 阿史那從禮說誘九姓府、六胡州諸胡數萬眾，聚於經略軍北，將寇朔方，上命郭子儀詣天德軍發兵討之。

translations.literal: Ashina Congli persuaded and enticed the various Hu of the Nine-Surname Prefecture and Six-Hu Prefectures—several tens of thousands—who gathered north of Jinglue Army and were about to raid Shuofang; the emperor ordered Guo Ziyi to go to Tiande Army to raise troops and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Congli persuaded tens of thousands of Hu from the Nine-Surname and Six-Hu prefectures to gather north of Jinglue Army and prepare to raid Shuofang. The emperor ordered Guo Ziyi to Tiande Army to raise troops and crush them.

sentences.zh: 左武鋒使僕固懷恩之子玢別將兵與虜戰，兵敗，降之；

translations.literal: Left Martial Vanguard Commissioner Pugu Huai'en's son Bin separately led troops to fight the barbarians; his army was defeated and he surrendered to them;
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Bin, son of Left Martial Vanguard Commissioner Pugu Huai'en, fought the enemy in a separate detachment, was defeated, and surrendered;

sentences.zh: 既而復逃歸，懷恩叱而斬之。

translations.literal: later he fled back again; Huai'en rebuked him and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: he later escaped and returned. Huai'en rebuked him and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 將士股慄，無不一當百，遂破同羅。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers trembled in their thighs; each fought as one against a hundred, and they thereupon broke the Tongluo.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers fought with such fury that each man seemed worth a hundred, and they routed the Tongluo.

sentences.zh: 上雖用朔方之眾，欲借兵於外夷以張軍勢，以豳王守禮之子承寀為敦煌王，與僕固懷恩使於回紇以請兵。

translations.literal: Though the emperor used the Shuofang host, he wished to borrow troops from foreign barbarians to swell military strength; he made Chengcai, son of Prince of Bin Shouli, Prince of Dunhuang, and with Pugu Huai'en sent him as envoy to the Uyghurs to request troops.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor relied on the Shuofang army, he wished to borrow troops from foreign powers to swell his strength. He made Chengcai, son of Prince of Bin Shouli, Prince of Dunhuang, and sent him with Pugu Huai'en as envoy to the Uyghurs to request troops.

sentences.zh: 又發拔汗那兵，且使轉諭城郭諸國，許以厚賞，使從安西兵入援。

translations.literal: He also mobilized Ferghana troops and had them relay word to the walled states and various kingdoms, promising rich rewards so they would follow the Anxi army in coming to aid.
translations.idiomatic: He also mobilized Ferghana troops and sent word through the oasis states, promising rich rewards if they would march in with the Anxi army to aid the cause.

sentences.zh: 李泌勸上：「且幸彭原，俟西北兵將至，進幸扶風以應之；

translations.literal: Li Mi urged the emperor, "For the present go to Pengyuan and wait until the northwestern troops are about to arrive, then advance to Fufeng to meet them;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi urged the emperor: "For now go to Pengyuan and wait until the northwestern troops are near, then advance to Fufeng to meet them;

sentences.zh: 於時庸調亦集，可以贍軍。」

translations.literal: at that time the corvée substitutes will also be gathered and can supply the army."
translations.idiomatic: by then the corvée tax substitutes will also have been gathered and can supply the army."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，發靈武。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen he departed Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day he departed Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 內侍邊令誠復自賊中逃歸，上斬之。

translations.literal: Inner Attendant Bian Lingcheng again fled back from among the rebels; the emperor had him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Attendant Bian Lingcheng fled back from the rebels again; the emperor had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 丙子，上至順化。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi the emperor reached Shunhua.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day the emperor reached Shunhua.

sentences.zh: 韋見素等至自成都，奉上寶冊，上不肯受，曰：「比以中原未靖，權總百官，豈敢乘危，遽為傳襲！」

translations.literal: Wei Jiansu and others arrived from Chengdu and presented the imperial treasure registers; the emperor would not accept them and said, "Lately, because the central plains are not yet pacified, I have provisionally taken charge of the hundred officials—how dare I seize this perilous moment and hastily accept succession!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiansu and others arrived from Chengdu and presented the imperial registers of investiture. The emperor refused them, saying, "Because the central plains are not yet pacified, I have provisionally taken charge of the hundred officials. How dare I seize this perilous moment and hastily accept the throne!"

sentences.zh: 群臣固請，上不許，置寶冊於別殿，朝夕事之，如定省之禮。

translations.literal: The ministers pressed their request firmly; the emperor would not agree and placed the treasure registers in a separate hall, attending them morning and evening with the rites of inquiry after his father's well-being.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed their request, but the emperor would not agree. He placed the registers in a separate hall and attended them morning and evening with the rites due a son inquiring after his father.

sentences.zh: 上以韋見素本附楊國忠，意薄之；

translations.literal: The emperor, because Wei Jiansu had originally attached himself to Yang Guozhong, held him in low regard;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held Wei Jiansu in low regard because he had originally attached himself to Yang Guozhong;

sentences.zh: 素聞房琯名，虛心待之，琯見上言時事，辭情慷慨，上為之改容，由是軍國事多謀於琯。

translations.literal: Jiansu had heard Fang Guan's reputation and received him with an open mind; Guan, on seeing the emperor, spoke on current affairs with impassioned words, and the emperor's expression changed for him—thereafter military and state affairs were largely planned with Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu had heard Fang Guan's reputation and received him with an open mind. Guan spoke to the emperor on current affairs with passionate urgency, and the emperor's expression changed. Thereafter military and state affairs were largely planned with Guan.

sentences.zh: 琯亦以天下為己任，知無不為，專決於胸臆；

translations.literal: Guan too took the empire as his own charge, doing whatever he knew should be done and deciding everything from his own breast;
translations.idiomatic: Guan too took the empire as his own charge, doing whatever he knew should be done and deciding everything from his own judgment;

sentences.zh: 諸相拱手避之。

translations.literal: the other chief ministers folded their hands and yielded before him.
translations.idiomatic: the other chief ministers folded their hands and yielded before him.

sentences.zh: 上皇賜張良娣七寶鞍，李泌言於上曰：「今四海分崩，當以儉約示人，良娣不宜乘此。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor bestowed on Consort Zhang Liangdi a saddle of seven treasures; Li Mi said to the emperor, "Now the four seas are sundered—we should show frugality to the people; the Consort should not ride this.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor bestowed on Consort Zhang Liangdi a saddle set with seven treasures. Li Mi said to the emperor, "The realm is sundered—we should show frugality to the people. The Consort should not ride this.

sentences.zh: 請撤其珠玉付庫吏，以俟有戰功者賞之。」

translations.literal: I ask that its pearls and jade be removed and given to the treasury clerks, to await rewarding those with military merit."
translations.idiomatic: Remove its pearls and jade and give them to the treasury, to reward those who earn merit in battle."

sentences.zh: 良娣自閣中言曰：「鄰里之舊，何至如是！」

translations.literal: The Consort spoke from within the pavilion, saying, "We are old neighbors—how can it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The Consort called from within the pavilion: "We are old neighbors—how can it come to this!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「先生為社稷計也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The gentleman is thinking of the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The gentleman is thinking of the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 遽命撤之。

translations.literal: He at once ordered it removed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it removed at once.

sentences.zh: 建寧王倓泣於廊下，聲聞於上；

translations.literal: Prince of Jianning Tan wept beneath the corridor, and his voice reached the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jianning Tan wept beneath the corridor, and his voice reached the emperor;

sentences.zh: 上驚，召問之，對曰：「臣比憂禍亂未已，今陛下從諫如流，不日當見陛下迎上皇還長安，是以喜極而悲耳。」

translations.literal: startled, the emperor summoned and asked him; he replied, "Your servant lately feared the turmoil would not end; now Your Majesty follows remonstrance like flowing water—in no many days we should see Your Majesty welcome the Retired Emperor back to Chang'an; therefore joy reached its extreme and turned to grief."
translations.idiomatic: Startled, the emperor summoned and asked him. Tan replied, "I lately feared the turmoil would never end. Now Your Majesty follows remonstrance like flowing water. Soon we shall see you welcome the Retired Emperor back to Chang'an. My grief is joy pushed past its limit."

sentences.zh: 良娣由是惡李泌及倓。

translations.literal: The Consort thereupon came to hate Li Mi and Tan.
translations.idiomatic: The Consort thereupon came to hate Li Mi and Tan.

sentences.zh: 上嘗從容與泌語及李林甫，欲敕諸將克長安，發其塚，焚骨揚灰。

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke at ease with Mi about Li Linfu and wished to order the generals, when Chang'an was taken, to open his tomb, burn his bones, and scatter his ashes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once spoke at ease with Mi about Li Linfu and wished to order the generals, when Chang'an was taken, to open his tomb, burn his bones, and scatter his ashes.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「陛下方定天下，奈何仇死者！

translations.literal: Mi said, "Your Majesty is just now settling the empire—why take vengeance on the dead!
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "Your Majesty is just now settling the empire—why take vengeance on the dead!

sentences.zh: 彼枯骨何知，徒示聖德之不弘耳。

translations.literal: What do those dry bones know? It would only show that sagely virtue is not broad.
translations.idiomatic: What do dry bones know? It would only show that your virtue is not magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 且方今從賊者皆陛下之仇也，若聞此舉，恐阻其自新之心。」

translations.literal: Moreover, those who now follow the rebels are all Your Majesty's enemies—if they hear of this act, I fear it will block their hearts from renewing themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who now follow the rebels are all your enemies. If they hear of this, I fear it will block their hearts from turning back."

sentences.zh: 上不悅，曰：「此賊昔日百方危朕，當是時，朕不保朝夕。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said, "This villain in former days endangered me in a hundred ways—at that time I could not be sure of morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said, "This villain endangered me in a hundred ways. At that time I could not be sure of morning or evening.

sentences.zh: 朕之全，特天幸耳！

translations.literal: That I survived was purely Heaven's fortune!
translations.idiomatic: That I survived was purely Heaven's fortune!

sentences.zh: 林甫亦惡卿，但未及害卿而死耳，奈何矜之！」

translations.literal: Linfu hated you too, but died before he could harm you—why pity him!"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu hated you too, but died before he could harm you—why pity him!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣豈不知！

translations.literal: He replied, "Does your servant not know this!
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Do I not know this!

sentences.zh: 所以言者，上皇有天下向五十年，太平娛樂，一朝失意，遠處巴蜀。

translations.literal: The reason I speak is that the Retired Emperor held the empire for nearly fifty years in peace and pleasure; in a single morning he lost his aim and was sent far to Ba-Shu.
translations.idiomatic: I speak because the Retired Emperor held the empire for nearly fifty years in peace and pleasure. In a single morning he lost everything and was sent far to Ba-Shu.

sentences.zh: 南方地惡，上皇春秋高，聞陛下此敕，意必以為用韋妃之故，內慚不懌。

translations.literal: The southern lands are harsh; the Retired Emperor's years are advanced; if he hears this edict of Your Majesty, he will surely think it is because of Consort Wei, and inwardly feel ashamed and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The southern lands are harsh, and the Retired Emperor is advanced in years. If he hears this edict, he will surely think it is because of Consort Wei and feel ashamed and displeased inwardly.

sentences.zh: 萬一感憤成疾，是陛下以天下之大，不能安君親。」

translations.literal: If by chance grief and anger turn to illness, then Your Majesty, with so great an empire, cannot give peace to father and kin."
translations.idiomatic: If grief and anger should turn to illness, then with so great an empire you cannot give peace to your father."

sentences.zh: 言未畢，上流涕被面，降階，仰天拜曰：「朕不及此，是天使先生言之也！」

translations.literal: Before he had finished speaking, the emperor wept until his face was covered, descended the steps, looked up to Heaven and bowed, saying, "I had not reached this thought—Heaven sent the gentleman to speak it!"
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the emperor wept until his face was covered. He descended the steps, looked up to Heaven, and bowed: "I had not reached this thought—Heaven sent you to speak it!"

sentences.zh: 遂抱泌頸泣不已。

translations.literal: He thereupon embraced Mi about the neck and wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He embraced Mi about the neck and wept without cease.

sentences.zh: 他夕，上又謂泌曰：「良娣祖母，昭成太后之妹也，上皇所念。

translations.literal: Another evening the emperor again said to Mi, "Consort Liangdi's grandmother was the younger sister of Empress Zhaocheng—one the Retired Emperor holds in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Another evening the emperor said to Mi again, "Consort Liangdi's grandmother was the younger sister of Empress Zhaocheng—someone the Retired Emperor holds dear.

sentences.zh: 朕欲使正位中宮，以慰上皇心，何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to make her the legitimate occupant of the inner palace to comfort the Retired Emperor's heart—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to make her empress to comfort the Retired Emperor's heart—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下在靈武，以群臣望尺寸之功，故踐大位，非私己也。

translations.literal: He replied, "When Your Majesty was at Lingwu, because the ministers hoped for some small measure of achievement, you ascended the great throne—not for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "When you were at Lingwu, you ascended the throne because the ministers hoped for some small measure of achievement—not for private ends.

sentences.zh: 至於家事，宜待上皇之命，不過晚歲月之間耳。」

translations.literal: As for household affairs, you should await the Retired Emperor's command—it will be no more than a matter of months and years."
translations.idiomatic: As for household affairs, you should await the Retired Emperor's command—it will be only a matter of months."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 南詔乘亂陷越巂會同軍，據清溪關；

translations.literal: Nanzhao seized the disorder to capture the Yuexi Huitong Army garrison and held Qingxi Pass;
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao seized the disorder to capture the Yuexi Huitong Army garrison and held Qingxi Pass;

sentences.zh: 尋傳、驃國皆降之。

translations.literal: soon afterward Xunchuan and Piaoguo both submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: soon afterward Xunchuan and Piaoguo both submitted to it.
